pages.content_excerpt: Postgraduate Admissions Admissions South Eastern Kenya University Postgraduate Admissions To be considered for postgraduate admission to South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU), you must meet minimum requirements set by the postgraduate School. Requirements of individual graduate programs are often more rigorous than those set by the postgraduate School. Every postgraduate program sets their own deadlines and requires the submission of additional materials. These materials vary by program, but examples include letters of reference, auditions, samples of your work, and personal statements. Information about required materials is available from the graduate coordinator of each program. Decisions regarding admission are made by the admitting departments, but all offers of admission are subject to verification of university admission requirements such as degree conferral, academic transcripts, etc., by postgraduate Admissions, Office of the University Registrar. When your application is complete, it will be reviewed on an individual basis by the School in your proposed program. headings: Alcohol, Drug and Substance Abuse Prevention
pages.content_excerpt: Alcohol, Drug and Substance Abuse Prevention The Alcohol and Drug Abuse (ADA) prevention unit was established through the South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU) Statutes. The core mandate of the unit includes development, implementation, evaluation and review of the University Alcohol and Drug Abuse Policy. The unit sensitizes SEKU Community on effects and prevention of alcohol drug and substance abuse, Dr.charles Orek implements a workplace Coordinator, ADSAP policy on use of alcohol and drug abuse, undertakes surveys to establish prevalence of alcohol and drug abuse and carry out an employer assistance programme focusing on early identification, treatment and rehabilitation. ADA prevention unit ensures adherence to prohibition of selling, advertising and drinking of alcohol as well as use, possession and distribution of drugs and controlled substances within the university premises by both students and staff members. pages.title: Career Services Unit
pages.content_excerpt: Career Services South Eastern Kenya University's Office of Career Services (OCS) was established in 2018 in response to a ministerial order to all universities to guide students on aspects of careers, career pathways and increase in employability. The office is mandated to mainstream provide services in student career and professional development. The areas of focus for the SEKU OCS include; Career guidance and counseling programmes Academic mentoring Graduate tracking Provision of career reference resources Increased training and industry exposure The OCS offers assistance to students in planning for immediate employment or post graduate studies in local or international institutions. To increase employability of graduates, the OCS conducts trainings in curriculum vitae writing, attending interviews, job etiquettes, professional ethics and emergence of international labour laws in the digital edge. Therefore, the OCS forms a vital link for a multidisciplinary platform to share and learn how to make a smooth transition from being mere students to being employees under different rules and regulations. The OCS provides such services to enable SEKU students to have a competitive edge

headings: Cohesion and National Values Mainstreaming Unit
pages.content_excerpt: Cohesion and National Values Mainstreaming Cohesion and National Values Mainstreaming Unit The National Values and Principles of Governance in Article 10 of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, epitomize the core beliefs and normative standards that steer the conduct of individuals and the functioning of institutions within Kenya. At South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU), these values are not just lofty ideals, but they are integrated principles that inform every aspect of the University’s operations. By embedding these values into its mandate, SEKU not only fulfills its constitutional obligations, but it also actively contributes to fostering a just and equitable society while tackling societal challenges sustainably. To ensure the seamless integration of these values into its mandate, SEKU has established a dedicated Cohesion and National Values Mainstreaming Unit. This Unit plays a pivotal role in coordinating training sessions and sensitization programmes, identifying the government’s commitments aligned with SEKU's mission, and advising the University Management on matters pertaining to national cohesion and values promotion. Moreover, it diligently prepares and submits Annual Pre

pages.title: Welcome To Board Of Postgraduate Studies
headings: Welcome To Board Of Postgraduate Studies
pages.content_excerpt: South Eastern Kenya University Admissions Welcome To Board Of Postgraduate Studies Welcome to the Board of Postgraduate studies at South Eastern Kenya University. The Board of Postgraduate Studies (BPS) is a service and administrative directorate that coordinates the formulation and development of postgraduate programs, admission of postgraduate students, student welfare matters and stimulates mutual engagement of staff and students in collaboration with the schools in the University. The Directorate strive to promote University excellence in postgraduate training, research and dissemination of research findings. The Mission of the Directorate is to provide high quality Postgraduate training opportunities with emphasis on Dry land Agriculture, Natural Resources Environmental Management, Science and information technology among other disciplines. The Directorate envisions itself to be nationally innovative for co-ordination of postgraduate training. Postgraduate programmes at SEKU have continued to grow, the current population of postgraduate students stands at 452 Masters and 95 PhD spread across different programmes in schools throughout the Main and Satellite University Campuses.

One of the key objectives of the University is to produce well educated, skilled and competent human capital through its academic programmes, and student welfare activities. A key strategy for realising this objective is the establishment of scholarship funds for disadvantaged students. pages.title: Gender Mainstreaming Unit
pages.content_excerpt: Gender Mainstreaming The Gender Mainstreaming Unit (GMU) at South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU) was formed in 2012 to respond to the growing needs of Gender mainstreaming within SEKU community. Since its inception the unit has made great strides. We have a functional gender mainstreaming committee and a coordinator. We have developed both the Gender Mainstreaming and Sexual and Gender based violence prevention policies which guide all our activities. As a higher institution of learning, we know that our growth and success will depend on how well we marshals the strengths of women and men to achieve our core mandate. The mission of the unit is to mainstream gender issues in all University policies, programmes, establishment and strengthening of existing partnerships and collaborations in gender and education. Our vision is an enabling environment where full potential of women and men both students and staff will be realized. Among our services include support to survivors of gender based discrimination and violence, advising the university on compliance to gender issues, organizing trainings and sensitizations on gender issues to both students and staff among other services. pages.title: HIV and AIDS Control Unit
pages.content_excerpt: HIV and AIDS Control HIV/AIDS has been one of the world's most serious public health challenges and sub-Saharan Africa has been the worst affected. The unit is concerned with issues relating to HIV/AIDS counselling, testing and post-testing services. It works closely with the University Health Unit, Student Counselling Unit as well as student peer counselors. The main activities of the SEKU HIV and Aids unit include: HIV Testing as the beginning of prevention. All are encouraged to know their status Counselling and post-testing care for students and staff, geared towards behaviour change Sensitization on HIV situation, facts, adherence to HIV treatment, relationship to other non-communicable diseases, reduction of stigma and discrimination On campus activities extends to ABCD of behaviour change, World AIDS Day celebrations, community outreach, continuous testing, counselling and post-testing care. The Unit continues to serve the SEKU fraternity through sensitizations on matters HIV; non communicable diseases: communicable diseases: Covid 19: mental health and the ABCD of behaviour change. How to Add or remove an account on Android Phones
pages.content_excerpt: How to Add or remove an account on Android Phones University Noticeboard How to Add or remove an account on Android Phones To access your email, contacts, and calendar, and to get apps from the Google Play Store, you can add accounts to your phone. When you add a Google account, info associated with that account automatically syncs with your phone. When you remove an account, everything associated with that account is also deleted from your phone. This includes email, contacts, and settings. Add a Google or other account to your phone Open your phone's Settings app. Tap Passwords & accounts. If you don't see "Accounts," tap Users & accounts. Under "Accounts for," tap Add account. To add your SEKU Email Account, tap Google. Follow the on-screen instructions. If you're adding accounts, you may need to enter your phone's pattern, PIN, or password for security. Remove a Google or other account from your phone Open your phone's Settings app. Tap Passwords & accounts. If you don't see "Accounts," tap Users & accounts. pages.content_excerpt: Postgraduate Admissions Admissions South Eastern Kenya University Postgraduate Admissions To be considered for postgraduate admission to South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU), you must meet minimum requirements set by the postgraduate School. Requirements of individual graduate programs are often more rigorous than those set by the postgraduate School. Every postgraduate program sets their own deadlines and requires the submission of additional materials. These materials vary by program, but examples include letters of reference, auditions, samples of your work, and personal statements. Information about required materials is available from the graduate coordinator of each program. Decisions regarding admission are made by the admitting departments, but all offers of admission are subject to verification of university admission requirements such as degree conferral, academic transcripts, etc., by postgraduate Admissions, Office of the University Registrar. When your application is complete, it will be reviewed on an individual basis by the School in your proposed program. pages.content_excerpt: Prospective Students Admissions South Eastern Kenya University Prospective Students The University indeed offers great opportunities for young people to realize their dreams and potentials. Our activities shall promote moral uprightness, respect, social and academic coherence. Some of the activities we would like to be involved in include: Promoting tolerance, understanding and ‘unity in diversity’ among students as a source of strength, Promoting awareness about HIV/AIDS, drug and substance abuse and other social issues impacting on students’ lives. Promoting environmental awareness among the student community as well as the local community, Promoting girl child education among members of the local community and demonstrating that ‘girls can do it’, Organizing visits and activities with the less fortunate members of the local community e.g. visiting children’s homes, hospitals, prisons etc. We look forward to everyone’s support Make the most of your time at South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU) by having an active and interesting student life.

pages.title: Resolution of public complaints unit
pages.content_excerpt: Resolution of Public Complaints South Eastern Kenya university has established the Resolution of Public Complaints Unit (RPCU) whose core function is to ensure timely and efficient resolution of complaints that may arise from the various service point within the institution. The Resolution of Complaints Committee liaises with the different departments in the university to ensure that complaints are resolved to the satisfaction of all the parties involved. The committee is under the chairmanship of the Deputy Vice Chancellor-Corporate Services and its membership is drawn from the different departments and sections of the university. The objectives of the RPCU are, among others: Establishment of the complaints handling and management infrastructure within the university, Conducting capacity building for complaints handling officers and staff, Creation of awareness on the existence of complaints handling system, and Resolution of complaints received and submitting quarterly report to the CAJ on the nature, number and actions taken. pages.content_excerpt: Directorates Board of Post Graduate Studies The Mission of the Directorate is to provide quality Postgraduate training opportunities with emphasis on dryland agriculture, natural resources and environmental management among other disciplines. The Board of Postgraduate Studies provides high quality services and programmes that promote the personal and professional development of diverse, non-traditional constituencies that internal and external to the University. The Directorate is mandated to provide and manage, postgraduate programmes in the University by co-coordinating, formulating and developing policies and programmes in collaboration with the schools in the University. It envisions itself as a globally innovative unit for co-ordination of postgraduate training. The current population of postgraduate students stands at 635 Masters and 91 PhD spread across different programmes in schools in all the Campuses. For admission into any of our postgraduate programmes, the admission forms can be downloaded from the South Eastern Kenya University Website. pages.title: Directorate of Academic Quality Assurance
pages.content_excerpt: Directorates Directorate of Academic Quality Assurance Prof. Peter G. Njuru, Director (AQA) In general terms, Quality Assurance (QA) can be defined as a systematic process that ensures the quality and reliability of a product or service; and involves creating and implementing processes, standards, and procedures to identify and correct any defects or deviations from the desired outcome. Academic Quality Assurance (AQA) therefore, refers to the processes and practices that ensure the quality and standards of teaching, learning, assessment, and research within the academic environment in an institution. The Directorate of Academic Quality Assurance is one of the directorates in SEKU and its core mandate is to oversee the development, implementation and review of relevant policies, procedures and regulations for academic quality assurance in the university. Under the directorate there exists the following sections Accomodation Our students are accommodated in the Main Campus. Both government sponsored and self-sponsored students are accommodated on a first come first served basis upon clearance on tuition and accommodation fees. Currently, SEKU has eight hostels, namely: Victoria, Turkwell, Elementaita, Athi, Baringo, Yatta, Magadi and Turkana. A number of the hostels have attached kitchens to serve the residents. Kitchen One serves the rest of the hostels. The students are served with well-prepared quality meals at affordable prices at the kitchens. The Directorate also runs a modern guest house with premier accommodation and quality catering services to our staff and other guests. pages.content_excerpt: Directorates Directorate of Strategy Quality and Performance Management Performance Contracting was introduced in Kenya’s public sector in 1991 as a tool for improving service delivery. The annual performance contracts are structured to align with the Kenya Vision 2030, Medium Term Plans, institutions strategic plan and annual work plan. SEKU has complied with the requirement of signing performance contracts with the parent ministry since 2008. During the last performance contract evaluation for financial year 2014/2015, the university achieved a composite score of 2.036 which is an excellent performance according to the Performance Contracting rating, thus putting SEKU among the best state corporations. The current contract has factored in some of the constitutional requirement such as national cohesion and integration, leadership and integrity. The performance contract has enabled the university to effectively execute its mandate and meet customer requirements. The Directorate, with a secretarial of three officers, is also charged with the responsibility of installing, maintaining and improving the quality systems within the university. headings: Technical Vocational Education and Training Admissions
Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Education
pages.content_excerpt: Admissions TVET Directorate Technical Vocational Education and Training Admissions The South Eastern Kenya University has a robust TVET Directorate under the experienced leadership of Dr. Selpher Cheloti. The University is accredited by TVETA to offer various Diploma and Certificate courses examined by Kenya National Examination Council (KNEC). The programs have been carefully selected to offer market driven training, impart industrial and entrepreneurial skills, lifelong learning and creative thinking, aiming job creation and employability of the TVET graduates of SEKU. We have Diplomas and Certificate courses in Engineering, ICT, Health sciences, Agriculture, Applied sciences, Business studies, Education and humanities. The programs are supported by well trained and experienced lecturers, state of the art training equipment and a well-equipped library in a serene learning environment. The University has well equipped Computer Laboratories and a vibrant Directorate of ICT to provide support infrastructure for research and E-learning. A variety of core curricula activities are also available to ensure wholesome development of our learners. The University has a well-trained guidance

Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Education
pages.content_excerpt: Directorate SEKU Directorates Technical Vocational Education and Training Directorate The South Eastern Kenya University has a dynamic TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training) Directorate. SEKU TVET Directorate is accredited by the Technical Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA), to offer training in Technical, Vocational Education and Training (TVET) at Diploma and Certificate levels. The directorate offers specialized training with practical, entrepreneurial, and industrial skills which is integrated with knowledge that is in line with National Development Agenda. The directorate offers diploma and certificate TVET courses across different schools such as School of Engineering and Technology, Education, Agriculture-environment -water and natural resources, Science and computing, Health sciences, Business and Economics, Humanities and social sciences. The programs are supported by well-trained academic and administrative staff training facilities including laboratories/workshops, a well-equipped library within a serene learning and training environment. pages.title: The Health Unit
pages.content_excerpt: The Health Unit SEKU Units The Health Unit A robust health service delivery centre is one of the most essential and important support service of any modern organization. This is why the university’s Health Unit endears itself to continually improve its services ranging from medical services, minor surgical procedures and antenatal clinics. The Health Unit in conjunction with the AIDS Control Unit has seen an increase in HIV testing from both students and staff members and reports are submitted to the Sub County Health On ce on the 5 th of every month with a view to supporting the Government’s to bring to control HIV/AIDS. In conjunction with the AIDS Control Unit, we have been able to organize health weeks where we invite experts from the health sector; for example, from 16 th to 20 th March, 2021, Equity Afya medical partnered with us in conducting full body check-ups to both our students and staff members. Th e health unit also worked hand in hand with Kitui Rural Sub County health team to sensitize and push for Covid-19 vaccination and testing in October 2021. pages.content_excerpt: Undergraduate Admissions Admissions South Eastern Kenya University Undergraduate Admissions Download | Admission letter South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU) offers a wide range of undergraduate courses within its campuses and collaborating centers. Personal cheques are not accepted.

Embracing innovation, flexibility and the future of higher education. Welcome to the Directorate of Open, Distance and e-Learning (ODeL) at South Eastern Kenya University (SEKU). Our university is committed to providing a dynamic educational experience that transcends traditional barriers, recognizing that learning can occur in diverse locations and moments. We are proud to announce the official rollout of Blended Learning beginning this semester. This innovative approach combines the strengths of face-to-face teaching with the flexibility of online learning, ensuring that our students receive a rich, interactive, and future-ready education. pages.content_excerpt: Overview BACKGROUND Dentistry is the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention and/or treatment (nonsurgical, surgical or related procedures) of diseases, disorders and/or conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area and/or the adjacent and associated structures and their impact on the human body. The diseases or conditions may be of hard and soft tissues and include tooth decay, infections, malformations, malocclusion, tumours and traumatic injuries. These conditions cause pain, discomfort, and morphological defects and impede normal function in the head and neck region. They may be debilitating and affect the social well-being of individuals thus impacting negatively on the quality of life. The Department of Dental Sciences, housed at the Dental School of the University of Nairobi, was established in 1974 to train dental practitioners and meet national development needs by providing oral healthcare services to the population. The Department has achieved this through the Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) programme as well as four flagship Master of Dental Surgery programmes in Paediatric Dentistry, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Prosthodontics and Periodontology. pages.content_excerpt: Overview CEC 31 – BACHELOR OF ECONOMICS 1.2 Philosophy The philosophy of economics concerns itself with conceptual, methodological, and ethical issues that arise within the scientific discipline of economics. The primary focus is on issues of methodology and epistemology—the methods, concepts, and theories through which economists attempt to arrive at knowledge about economic processes. Philosophy of economics is also concerned with the ways in which ethical values are involved in economic reasoning—the values of human welfare, social justice, and the tradeoffs among priorities that economic choices require. Economic reasoning has implications for justice and human welfare; more importantly, economic reasoning often makes inexplicit but significant ethical assumptions that philosophers of economics have found it worthwhile to scrutinize. Finally, the philosophy of economics is concerned with the concrete social assumptions that are made by economists. 1.3 Rationale Economics governs the life of the individual, Society and the modern States. pages.content_excerpt: Overview Introduction Background Agriculture is the backbone of Kenya’s economy. It contributes about 30% of the GDP and provides income to over 70% of the population. However, the sector continues to face many challenges, one of them being lack of skilled manpower. There is need for manpower which can effectively generate and promote technologies, strategies and services that can enhance agricultural productivity and quality while preserving the environment as envisaged in national’s Vision 2030 and as spelt out in the Agricultural Sector Development Strategy (ASDS). The degree in Agricultural Education and Extension will prepare graduates for education and leadership positions in agriculture including extension, teaching in secondary schools and tertiary institutions. The curriculum is fairly broad and offers many career opportunities in education and agriculture. Duration and Structure of the Programme
The program shall run over a minimum of two semesters equivalent to one academic year.
The program shall be by coursework and a research project.

Assessment shall be based on the final examination and continuous assessment based on written assignments, seminar presentations, continuous assessment and such other tests given during the course. The final examination in each course shall count for 70% and continuous assessments for 30% of the total marks.

The Ph.D. in Nursing program prepares the students for the leadership role to design a unique research project involving innovations, discovery, Theory development, policy development, and knowledge translation to practice that will contribute to a lifelong program in nursing. Students also develop skills in the analytical ability to collaborate on intra-professional projects. The curriculum enriches learning through social, behavioral, and biological sciences. Anchoring these advances in the curriculum will guarantee quality graduates who match global standards. This applies to the University of Nairobi policy that all PhDs be provided through coursework and Thesis. The doctoral program is intended to enhance individuals' capacity and skills for positions involving teaching, research, and Leadership role in local and international institutions.

pages.content_excerpt: Overview Chronic noncommunicable diseases including KD are causing significant morbidity and mortality in developing countries, Kenya included. This public health problem has affected quality of life of those affected and has also increased the financial burden of Kenyans. The Rapid Response Teams for this problem are found mainly in the referral hospitals. As such the services are inaccessible to majority of the needy Kenyans. With the devolved health care governance, equipping health care facilities with competent health personnel is critical. At present these institutions lack the human capacity to manage and run the state of the art technology facilities and services. This programme is therefore aimed at bringing the capacity gaps by training nurses to enable them offer collaborative management to clients suffering from renal disorders. pages.content_excerpt: Home About Us Explore UoN Awards & Achievements Higher Doctorate Degrees Those eligible for the award of a Higher Doctorate of the University of Nairobi must among other requirements be holders of the Doctor of Philosophy or Doctor of Medicine degree of the University of Nairobi or the Doctor of Philosophy degree from any other recognized university of at least five years standing. The Common Regulations for Higher Doctorates of the University of Nairobi other than Honorary Degrees are set out in the University Calendar. The Higher Doctorate, the regulations stipulate, shall only be awarded for the original published work such as would give a candidate authoritative international standing in his/her particular field of research. The application must be based wholly or substantially on original work of distinction carried out by the candidate. The term ‘‘published’’ shall mean printed in a referred journal, book or monograph which shall have been made available to the public. pages.content_excerpt: Overview The provision of quality nursing care is paramount in prevention of disease, promotion of health and management of diseases, in hospitals and communities. In Kenya, the Nursing Profession is in need of nurses trained at higher levels to take up positions in clinical practice, research, and teaching. The department of Nursing Science was established to train students for Diploma in Advanced Nursing in 1968. This programme graduated several generations of candidates from Kenya and abroad. The diploma graduates worked in the private and public sectors as Nurses, Teachers, and Nurse Managers both in Kenya and abroad. In 1992, a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BScN) Programme was started. Several graduates have gone through the programme in the department. These nurses continue to work in this country and abroad in both public and private hospitals, and other institutions. In Kenya, there is no institution of higher learning offering a higher degree at Master of Science in Nursing (MSc.N), and there are only a few such institutions in the African region. pages.content_excerpt: The University of Nairobi, a body corporate established under the Universities Act No. 42 of 2012 and the University of Nairobi Charter, 2013 The Department of Nursing Sciences was established in 1968 as the Department of Advanced Nursing under the Faculty of Medicine. In the year 2006, it became a School of Nursing Sciences under the College of Health Sciences . With the governance reforms currently at the University of Nairobi, it was renamed the Department of Nursing Sciences headed by the Chairman of Department. The Department has four (4) Thematic units namely: Medical Surgical Nursing, Obstetrics /Midwifery and Gynaecological Nursing, Community Health Nursing and Nursing Education & Administration.

pages.content_excerpt: I am delighted to welcome you to the prestigious Department of Nursing Sciences of the University of Nairobi on behalf of the faculty and staff. To the students who come from outside the capital city and Kenya, I wish to welcome you to Nairobi. The Department of Nursing Sciences is one of the departments of the Faculty of Health Sciences. Over the years, the programs of the department have expanded to include Diploma in Renal Nursing, BScN upgrading courses, Master of Science, and Doctor of Philosophy in Nursing. As a department, we are proud of our national and international reputation in producing high-caliber clinical nurse practitioners, educators, managers, and researchers who are highly respected and hold high status in society. The department is located within Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) campus and comprises four Thematic Units. These are Administration and Education, Community Health Nursing, Medical–Surgical Nursing and Midwifery, and Obstetrics nursing. pages.content_excerpt: Home About Us Explore UoN Awards & Achievements Honorary Degrees An honorary degree, honoris causa which is Latin: ‘for the sake of the honor’, is an academic degree for which a university or a degree-awarding institution has waived the usual requirements like the sitting of examinations. An honorary degree is a doctorate, awarded to individuals who have no prior connection with the institution in question. The conferring of an honorary degree is the greatest honor that any University can bestow to a person. The degree is usually conferred as a way of honoring a distinguished person’s contributions to a specific field, or to society in general. Honorary degrees are usually awarded at regular graduation ceremonies, at which the recipients are invited to make an acceptance speech before the assembled faculty and graduates – an event which forms the highlight of the graduation ceremony. This practice dates back to the Middle Ages, when for various reasons a university would be persuaded, or otherwise deem it fit, to grant exemption from some or all of the usual statutory requirements for the award of a degree. pages.content_excerpt: #MyANU What begins here, transforms the world APPLY HERE Explore ANU RESEARCH ALUMNI RECREATION AND SPORTS ANU is for you! Our Mission is to provide a holistic education that equips individuals with excellent skills, competencies, and Christian Values. Our Vision is to be the university of choice for individuals desiring Christ-centered academic excellence and transformative leadership. student life RESEARCH ALUMNI RECREATION AND SPORTS Explore our Majors & Programs School of Law School of Business School of Science and Technology School of Humanities and Social Sciences School of Religion and Christian Ministry School of Law School of Business School of Science and Technology School of Humanities and Social Sciences School of Religion & Christian Ministry Main Campus The main campus is situated in the middle of the great Masaai savannah on 124 acres next to the Nairobi National Park, off Magadi Road near Ongata Rongai Town, 24km from the Nairobi City Center The University offers a peaceful and tranquil environment with well-manicured, plush gardens. pages.content_excerpt: Welcome Message Revd. Charles O. Onyango Head, Non-Degree Academic Programmes Welcome to ANU Non-Degree Academic Programmes Skills that Open Doors. Qualifications that Create Possibilities. Welcome to Africa Nazarene University’s Non-Degree Academic Programmes, where practical skills become real opportunities. The world of work is changing. Employers need people who can do , not simply people who know. Whether you are preparing for employment, advancing your career, changing direction, strengthening your professional skills, or preparing for further study, our Diploma and Certificate Programmes are designed to give you the knowledge, practical competence and confidence to move forward. Why ANU? Practical Skills. Real-World Relevance. Gain skills designed for today’s workplace and applicable beyond the classroom. Flexible Pathways. Learning that Fits Your Life. Choose face-to-face or online learning, with intakes in January , May and August . Build your qualifications progressively through pathways that allow you to keep learning and advancing. pages.content_excerpt: Programs Offered in Africa Nazarene University School of Law School of Business School of Science and Technology School of Humanities and Social Sciences School of Religion & Christian Ministry Bachelor of Laws Bachelor of Arts Criminal Justice and Security Management The School of Law at Africa Nazarene University offers a dynamic and rigorous Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) programme designed to open diverse and rewarding career pathways within and beyond the legal profession. Graduates are well-prepared to pursue professional legal training and qualification as advocates, leading to careers in legal practice as litigators, corporate lawyers, or in specialized fields such as commercial law, human rights, and international law. The programme also provides a strong foundation for careers in the judiciary, prosecution, and public service, as well as roles within regulatory bodies, non-governmental organizations, and international institutions. For those inclined toward academia, policy, or research, the LL.B. offers a solid platform for postgraduate study and scholarly engagement. pages.content_excerpt: January 2027 Intake Ongoing Apply Now Skip to content Diploma in Nursing: Pre-service KRCHN Programme (Fresh entry) Course Overview The Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN) – Pre-service at Amref International University (AMIU) is a comprehensive three-year, full-time residential programme designed for high school graduates aspiring to become professional nurses. Delivered through face-to-face instruction, the curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical clinical experience, focusing on areas such as medical-surgical nursing, maternal and child health, community health, mental health, and pharmacology. The programme emphasizes evidence-based practice and cultural competence, preparing graduates to provide high-quality, patient-centered care across diverse healthcare settings. Intakes occur in April and August, and both resident and day scholars are welcome. pages.content_excerpt: January 2027 Intake Ongoing Apply Now Skip to content Malaria Diagnostic Refresher Training (MDRT) Course Course Overview Laboratory confirmation of malaria infection is an essential component of fever case management and should be provided at all levels of health care to ensure correct patient management and minimise the use and cost of anti-malarial treatment drugs. The Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030 was adopted by the World Health Assembly in May 2015 with the aim of achieving a malaria-free world by 2030. To achieve these goals countries must adopt policies and practices that improve the quality of laboratory confirmation of malaria diagnosis. This will retain the confidence of clinicians in laboratory results, leading to improved case management and appropriate use of antimalarial drugs. The course is approved by the KMLTTB for the award of 50 CPD points COURSE OBJECTIVES i. To improve the quality of malaria microscopy and essential malaria diagnostic procedures, including use of malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDT) ii. pages.content_excerpt: Faculty of Education Transforming Education Through Excellence and Innovation The Faculty of Education at The Catholic University of Eastern Africa is dedicated to preparing competent, innovative, and ethical educators who will transform education across Eastern Africa and beyond. Our programs emphasize both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, ensuring our graduates are well-equipped to address contemporary educational challenges in diverse learning environments. Through cutting-edge research, community engagement, and partnerships with educational institutions, we contribute to educational policy development and best practices in the region. Dean, Faculty of Education: Prof. Peter Koros Welcome to the Faculty of Education at The Catholic University of Eastern Africa. Our faculty is committed to excellence in teacher preparation, educational leadership, and transformative research that addresses the evolving needs of education in Eastern Africa and beyond. We offer comprehensive programs that blend theoretical knowledge with practical experience, preparing educators who are not only skilled practitioners but also reflective scholars capable of driving educational innovation

pages.content_excerpt: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences Established in 1989, shaping minds through diverse academic offerings in seven specialized departments The Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences was established in 1989 and is one of the oldest academic faculties at CUEA. Our scholars and researchers guide students through fascinating course topics, personalized degree programs, and numerous research opportunities across diverse fields of study. The Faculty comprises seven full-fledged academic departments: Development Studies, English, Geography and Environmental Science, History, Kiswahili, Religious Studies, Philosophy, Social Sciences, and Foreign Languages. We offer certificate, diploma, and degree programs designed to meet the diverse intellectual interests of our students. Our programs are carefully designed and constantly reviewed in consultation with stakeholders to support student career goals and prepare them for graduate studies. Faculty advisors support students every step of the way, creating a fulfilling academic experience grounded in leadership, passion, and curiosity about research and teaching. Dean, Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences: Dr. Muchoki Francis Macharia (Ph.D.) Welcom

pages.content_excerpt: Faculty of Law Producing competent and morally conscious law graduates with requisite legal skills who deliver quality legal service. The Faculty of Law, now celebrating 20 years of existence began in the year 2005 as a Department within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. The Department was responsible for managing the Bachelor of Laws degree programme which had been launched in March of the same year as well as teaching various law courses in other faculties at the University. In 2007, the Department transformed into the Faculty of Law and was formally inaugurated during the Universityâs Convocation on 25th August 2007. Located at the Kozlowiecki Hall, situated along Bogani East Road in Langâata, Nairobi, the Faculty has a space and serene facility which accommodates its faculty and administration offices, lecture hall and rooms, computer lab, a moot court facility and student leadership offices. The facility is accessible to people living with disabilities and provides necessary amenities for them. There is ample parking space and good security. Our programs are designed to develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and scientific inquiry, preparing graduates to address real-world challenges and contribute to scientific advancement. pages.title: Faculty of Theology | CUEA
pages.content_excerpt: Faculty of Theology Producing Innovative Graduates for the Church and Society The CUEA Faculty of Theology is under the direction of the Holy See, governed by the Apostolic Constitution Veritatis Gaudium and grants ecclesiastical degrees. The Faculty collaborates closely with the Congregation for Catholic Education â Rome, producing innovative graduates for the Church and Society. The graduates are employed in Church institutions, seminaries and houses of formation. The Faculty which attracts students from AMECEA region and beyond has continued its tradition of quality research and publishing through the Faculty Journal, African Christian Studies. The journal attracts researchers from within and outside the Faculty and CUEA Faculty members actively participate in conferences, seminars, public lectures and workshops in and outside the University. The Faculty has also published quality books under the series, Studies in African Christian Theology. The Faculty Interdisciplinary Theological Session is held every year and proceedings are published. Dean, Faculty of Theology: Rev. Prof. Richard N. pages.title: School of Business and Economics | CUEA
pages.content_excerpt: School of Business and Economics Building tomorrow's business leaders through excellence in education and research Welcome to the School of Business and Economics at the Catholic University of Eastern Africa. The Bachelor of Commerce degree program started in 1991. Between 1991 and 2002, students were admitted to the Department of Commerce and Business Administration (CBA) in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. The School of Business was inaugurated on 25th August 2003, then referred to as Faculty of Commerce. The School has three departments: Department of Accounting and Finance, Department of Marketing and Management, and Department of Management Science. The departments offer jointly; ordinary diploma in business management, advanced diploma in Business Management and Bachelor of Commerce degree program, with specializations in Accounting, Finance, Banking and Financial Services, Marketing, Management, and Human Resource Management. The School also has a Graduate Business School, offering a Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree program with specializations in E-commerce, Human Resource Management, Strategic Management, Marketing, Finance, and Entrepreneurship. The

pages.title: School of Graduate Studies | CUEA
pages.content_excerpt: School of Graduate Studies Transforming Scholars, Shaping Leaders Welcome to the CUEA School of Graduate Studies. The office of Graduate Studies at CUEA is committed to providing University-level oversight to ensure the quality of the graduate experience and maintain the integrity of activities relating to graduate studies, guided by our motto: âConsecrate them in the truthâ, John 17:17. Vision: To become a model of excellence and accomplishment in graduate studies in molding transformative leaders for Church and Society. Mission: To promote a diverse community of scholars among students and faculty members in order to foster a culture of excellence and integrity in graduate studies through innovation, research and creative expression of knowledge. Director, School of Graduate Studies: Rev. Dr. Paul Mathenge Rev. Dr. Paul Mathenge is the Director of the School of Graduate Studies, the Manager of the CUEA Innovation Hub and a lecturer at the School of Business and Economics. He holds a doctorate in Business Administration and Management - Entrepreneurship Studies. Rev. Dr. Paul Mathenge â Director, Graduate Rev. pages.title: School of Nursing | CUEA
pages.content_excerpt: School of Nursing Transforming Healthcare Through Compassionate Care I am delighted to welcome you to the Catholic University of Eastern Africa (CUEA) School of Nursing. Our mission is to provide exceptional nursing education that prepares compassionate, competent, and ethical healthcare professionals. The School of Nursing at CUEA is committed to excellence in nursing education, research, and community service. We strive to produce graduates who will make significant contributions to healthcare delivery in the region and beyond. Vision: To be a center of excellence in nursing education, research and practice in the service of the Church and society. Mission: To provide quality nursing education and training that prepares competent, compassionate and ethical nurses who will contribute to the improvement of health care in the Church and society. pages.content_excerpt: This programme aims at equipping students with practical skills of operating travel companies and hospitality operations. Taught skills include: itinerary planning, travel scheduling, tour packaging, air fare calculation, ticketing, fleet management and tour guiding. The hospitality skills include; front office operations, housekeeping operations, food and beverage production and service. We equip students with practical operational skills to enable them work at middle management levels. The target groups of the programme are suitable qualified candidates who would like to develop a career in tourism, travel, and airline and hotel businesses.

pages.content_excerpt: Welcome to the Faculty of Science and Technology (FAST) where our commitment is to offer programs and solutions that are not only relevant to the rapidly evolving market and technological landscape but also to craft a way for the future. At the Faculty of Science and Technology, we focus on the sciences, technology, and innovation. Faculty of Science and Technology at Chuka University develops and disseminates knowledge, creates new technological inventions for sustainable development, and solutions to world problems.

pages.content_excerpt: Bachelor of Arts in Monitoring and Evaluation Enroll for this course today About Course Rationale This is a skills based course aimed at equipping the student with the appropriate capacity to pursue a career in monitoring and evaluation. It is designed to present the requisite information that will enhance the students’ knowledge and skills needed to effectively impact on project management processes. Requirements Applicants to the Bachelor of Arts in Monitoring and Evaluation must fulfil entry requirements that apply to all Daystar undergraduate students, i.e. An overall minimum grade of C+ in KCSE or at least 4 credits in IGCSE with at least 2 credit passes at 'A' level/GCE . pages.content_excerpt: Bachelor of Arts in Peace & Conﬂict Transformation Enroll for this course today About Course Rationale The purpose of this program is to integrate theory and practice with a view to preparing students to serve as change agents in war torn societies in Africa and the world. The Peace and Conflict Transformation (PCT) program recognizes conflict as an inevitable phenomenon in human relationships. It emphasizes on the transformation of conflicts and the development of non-violent mechanisms of responding to conflicts. In addition, the Programme is concerned with factors and conditions that make peace and justice possible including the promotion and protection of human rights, human security, and the causes of poverty and injustices in Africa. Requirements Applicants to the Bachelor of Arts in Peace & Conﬂict Transformation must fulfil entry requirements that apply to all Daystar undergraduate students, i.e. An overall minimum grade of C+ in KCSE or at least 4 credits in IGCSE with at least 2 credit passes at 'A' level/GCE . It is a very ‘real-world’ discipline that has produced Biomedical research scientists who have made global and national headlines with advances in their fields, with results that you can see first-hand such as growing embryos for IVF to answer the challenges of infertility, 3D-printing of a heart to alleviate cardiovascular disorders or developing a new medicine to fight cancer and HIV/AIDS and vaccine development to combat Corona virus pandemic. Discovery of new drugs and therapies requires careful scientific ethics, experimentation, development, and evaluation and this is a major part of our program training. pages.content_excerpt: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Health BSc. (Environmental Health) is a preventive medicine - and intervention- focused major that aims to protect, prolong and promote health among the populations. Disease etiology, individual factors, environmental factors, cultural influences, and strategies for addressing and understanding vulnerable groups are studied in this major. It is a complementary field to medical training; indeed where public health programs are effective, prevalence of disease goes down and the population is much healthier. Requirements A mean grade of C+ (plus) and above in KCSE, or 5 credits in IGCSE with 2 credits passes in A level or division 2 in GCE. Course description Healthcare leaders agree that “prevention of diseases is better than cure” hence BSc. (Environmental Health) is a leading medically inclined major in both developed and developing countries since it is directed towards making the population healthier through preventing diseases and providing intervention services. pages.content_excerpt: Diploma in Disability Studies Enroll for this course today About Course Program Description A diploma in interdisciplinary disability studies will lead to knowledge, skills and competencies to launch a new career, or to add to an unrelated degree or certificate. The purpose is to meet national or state qualifications to venture into disability studies. The diploma program is a progressive curriculum with 60-credit-hour programs in which individuals from varied disciplines and professional backgrounds study together to gain knowledge and skills in disability theory, policy, service and research and practice. It provides an overview, investigates, critiques and enhances understanding of disability and provides specialization. The disability studies program will introduce learners to critical frameworks that will enhance their understanding of disadvantages and exclusions experiences arising from personal and societal responses to impairment. pages.content_excerpt: Home Welcome Message Programmes About PBL PBL Process Board Members Main Web : admissions@daystar.ac.ke : +254 709 972 000 | + 254 716 170 313 E-learning Student Portal Covid19 Updates Support DU Projects What's PBL Home > What's PBL What's PBL Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centred approach in which students engage in collaborative group learning to explore and solve real-life problems. PBL is based on the principle of using problems as a beginning point to academic inquiry. Problem-Based Learning (PBL) approach differs from the traditional lecture teaching method in which the lecturer leads in the transmission of knowledge. Contrary to the latter, the PBL approach empowers learners with the opportunity to take the lead in discovering and sharing of knowledge and skills through problem solving. In PBL, learners work in small groups where they are presented with real-world problems and exposed to practical hands-on training. The lecturer assumes the role of a facilitator while leaners are encouraged and motivated to use their innovative and creative thinking skills to develop practical solutions to the problems at hand. pages.content_excerpt: Diploma and Certificate Programmes Diploma in Sustainable Tourism & Hospitality Management This Two (2) years Programme seeks to equip learners with technical knowledge, skills and competencies that will enable them to contribute effectively to the sustenance and growth of tourism and hospitality industry through the application of sustainability principles in operations, product development, packaging, marketing and customer satisfaction management. After training the trainee should be able to: Apply technical knowledge, skills and attitudes for effective development and management of sustainable tourism and hospitality ventures. Develop and produce different types of foods and beverages to the required standards of catering and accommodation establishment. Apply the principles of professional tour guiding and interpretation. Apply the principles of cost control in order to minimize cost and maximize profit. Demonstrate an understanding of the various components of tourism and hospitality sectors. He has served as an Officer in charge of managing the American Military Aid to Kenya, an Officer in Charge of the Research Department at Defence Headquarters, and Commander of an Air Defence Battalion in Kenya Air Force. He served as a Liaison Officer in Sarajevo (Bosnia), a Senior Military Liaison Officer in Belgrade (Serbia), and a Senior Military Observer in Belgrade and Croatia, all with the United Nations as a peacekeeper in 1992/93. pages.content_excerpt: Our Profile Dedan Kimathi University of Technology (DeKUT) was established under the University’s Act 2012 by the Government of Kenya in December 2012. It is a Public University that focuses on Quality Education, Research, Innovation, Technology Development and Transfer. The University is a successor of Kimathi University College of Technology (KUCT), a constituent college of Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT). Before KUCT, the University was an institute going by the name Kimathi Institute of Technology (KIT) established by the community with the focus of building on education and technology to better the society; a heritage the University has held to this point and lives by. The University offers a wide range of programmes both at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels in various Schools and Institutes. The programmes are spread across Engineering, Health & Applied Sciences, Business Management and Economics, Computing, Food Science and Technology, Leather Technology, Geothermal Energy Technology, Geomatics, Geospatial Information Systems and Remote Sensing, Tourism and Hospitality, Criminology and Forensics Management, Technical and Professional St

pages.content_excerpt: WHY DeKUT IS NAMED AFTER DEDAN KIMATHI WACHIURI ABOUT DEDAN KIMATHI WACHIURI Dedan Kimathi Wachiuri was born on 31 st October 1920 and died on 18 th February 1957. He was a liberation leader who fought against the British colonial government in Kenya in the 1950s. He was convicted and executed in 1957 for murder and terrorism. The British colonial government that ruled Kenya considered him as a terrorist, as did the many Kenyans who opposed the Mau Mau. Former Mau Mau viewed Kimathi as a freedom fighter, although many of the kikuyu viewed him as a terrorist, due to the predations of the Mau Mau and the atrocities committed by the Mau Mau upon them. A particularly good source of turned agents for the government faces were those former Mau Mau escaping from justice handed out by Kimathi, which was followed by death by strangulation. The capture of Kimathi was headed by the unknown knowledge and skills because of the vast areas of rough terrain which hid the Mau Mau and Kimathi. pages.content_excerpt: DeKUT Launces Exchange Program with Toulouse INP (Institut National Polytechnique de Toulouse), France The Vice Chancellor of DeKUT, Prof. Eng. Peter Muchiri, EBS led a delegation to INP Toulouse, France to launch the Erasmus KA-171 Mobility project between DeKUT and INP Toulouse, which will benefit Bachelors, Masters and PhD students in Micro-Electronics Engineering, Food Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering among other disciplines. This will greatly strength the existing MoU with DeKUT and open up the collaboration beyond the Double Degree arrangement with ENSEEIHT on ESECA. The team visited the three main campuses of INP Toulouse and confirmed the key potential areas for expanding our collaboration in joint training, research and technology transfer.

Dedan Kimathi University of Technology (DeKUT) is a public, coeducational technological University in Kenya. It was the first university in Kenya to be chartered under the new universities’ act of 2012 and the eighth public university to be established in the country. Where is the main campus located? Dedan Kimathi University of Technology Main Campus is located 6 km from Nyeri town along Nyeri- Nyahururu highway, 160 kilometers North of Nairobi City. How can I apply? All applicants must complete an application form online through our website ( www.dkut.ac.ke ) or download the form and submit to the Registrar (Academic Affairs) Private Bag, Dedan Kimathi, Nyeri, Kenya, Tel: 061- 2050000. How should I submit my application material? Submit to the Registrar (Academic Affairs) P.O Box 657-10100, Nyeri or upload when applying online. How do I check my application status? pages.content_excerpt: Full license Recognition of Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics by KNDI DeKUT is pleased to announce the full license recognition of the Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics program by Kenya Nutritionists and Dieticians Institute (KNDI). This recognition is a testament to the University’s commitment to academic excellence and the delivery of quality, industry-relevant programs. The accreditation by the professional body (KNDI) underscores the credibility of our academic programs, ensuring that our graduates are well-equipped with the knowledge, skills, and competencies required in the field of nutrition and dietetics. It further positions DeKUT as a leading institution in producing qualified professionals who meet the national and global standards. This milestone reaffirms our dedication to upholding academic quality and fostering innovation in health sciences education. As we continue to enhance our programs, we remain committed to empowering our students with the expertise needed to make significant contributions to the nutrition and dietetics profession in Kenya and beyond.

pages.content_excerpt: Information Materials on Persons With Disabilities(PWDs) Home Home Dedan Kimathi University of Technology (DeKUT) is committed to ensuring that all our students and staff are treated equitably. Though there exists some entrenched ways of supporting students with a wide range light impairments, recent legislations and international conventions have required that the University improves yet further upon our provision and reappraise all our practices to ensure that they not unintentionally discriminatory or present unnecessary barriers to PWDs. The University is committed to working towards understanding and applying the Social Model of Disability, thereby not focusing on an individual’s medical condition or impairment, but instead identifying the impact of Disability in the structural, organizational, physical and attitudinal barriers that prohibit disabled people from achieving equality and inclusion of their needs, rights and requirements. DeKUT developed and promulgated the 1st Disability Mainstreaming Policy in 2010 and later revised in 2017. Animal Science and Technology Admission requirements Candidates wishing to pursue a BSc. degree program in Animal Science and Technology must meet the minimum admission requirements of Egerton University. In addition a candidate should have KCSE mean grade of C+ (plus) or its equivalent, C+ (plus) in English/Kiswahili, and C in Mathematics/Physics, Biology/Agriculture and Chemistry. Diploma with at least a credit in Animal Science, Animal Health, Agriculture, Range Management and related disciplines from institutions recognized by Egerton University Senate OR Diploma with a pass and at least two years relevant working experience OR A level certificate with a minimum of two principal passes and one subsidiary pass in relevant subjects. Duration BSc. Animal Science and Technology is a four-year program on full time study mode.

pages.content_excerpt: Students AI Policies Programmes Education Financing Portal Library Downloads Gallery Lord Egerton Castle Staff profiles Scholarships for Academic Excellence An Endowment Fund Scholarships for Undergraduate students at Egerton University has been established. This is part of the initiatives by the Egerton University Endowment Fund setup in the year 2007 to provide scholarship to bright but needy students in the continuing years. According to a communique from the office of the Vice- Chancellor, applications are invited from qualified candidates for scholarships (Tuition and Accommodation). Eligibility for awards includes: Must be joint admission board (JAB) students, self sponsored students are not eligible. Must be continuing student in 2nd year and above. Have exemplary academic performance with a minimum and sustained Cumulative Weighted Average of 70.00 (First Class Honors) Proof of need as evidenced by needs assessment report from the dean of students Interested students should send their applications to the Director, Board of Undergraduate Studies and Attachment Programmes enclosing the following: Certified copies of the previous year (s)provisional transcripts. If you can think of a study field or career that suits your personality, interests, goals and what you’re good at, you will enjoy what you do and being really great at your studies and future career. The University currently has over fifty-one (52) academic departments that offer a wide range of programmes at the diploma, undergraduate, and postgraduate levels. The departments are spread over 10 faculties namely Agriculture, Arts and Social Sciences, Commerce, Education and Community Studies, Engineering and Technology, Environment and Resources Development, Health Sciences, Science, Law and Veterinary Medicine and Surgery. It prepares qualified scholars and educators capable of utilizing Quranic guidance in the fields of education, outreach, guidance, and community reform, according to a scientific methodology that combines sound legal principles with practical application. The program is considered a pioneering initiative that contributes to spreading the culture of contemplation and activating the impact of the Holy Quran on the lives of individuals and communities. pages.title: Directorate of Student Support Services (DSSS)
pages.content_excerpt: Dr. Mary Onditi Director View Profile About us Functions Departments The Directorate of Student Support Services (DSSS) at JOOUST is dedicated to providing a comprehensive range of services that support the academic and personal development of students. DSSS offers guidance and counseling, career services, academic advising, and health and wellness programs to help students navigate their university experience successfully. By addressing the diverse needs of students, the directorate ensures that they have the resources and support necessary to achieve their academic and personal goals. In addition to individual support services, DSSS organizes a variety of programs and activities that promote student engagement and community building. These include orientation sessions for new students, leadership development programs, extracurricular activities, and cultural events. By fostering a vibrant and inclusive campus life, DSSS enhances the overall student experience and contributes to the development of well-rounded individuals who are prepared to make positive contributions to society. As a key academic division of the university, the BPS provides leadership in the development, coordination, and administration of postgraduate programs across various disciplines. Our Mandate The Board of Postgraduate Studies is responsible for overseeing all postgraduate programs at JOOUST, ensuring high academic and research standards in line with national and international best practices. Our core functions include: Admission and Registration Program Development & Review Research Coordination Quality Assurance Supervision and Examination At BPS, we are dedicated to nurturing a dynamic intellectual environment that promotes advanced scholarship, critical thinking, and innovation. We work closely with faculties, schools, and research centers to provide postgraduate students with the resources and mentorship they need to thrive in academia, industry, and society. pages.title: University Graduation
headings: How to Put on Academic Robes for a Graduation Ceremony
pages.content_excerpt: INSTRUMENTS OF POWER Mace The mace is a ceremonial staff carried by a university official, usually the mace bearer. It is made of wood or metal and adorned with intricate designs and symbols. Academic robes These are worn by the graduates, professors, and other university officials during the ceremony. The robes are usually black or dark blue and have distinctive colors and patterns on the sleeves and hoods to signify the graduate's field of study or degree level. Caps and hoods Graduates wear caps and hoods that correspond to their academic degree, with different colors and shapes representing different fields of study. The hoods are draped over the graduates' shoulders and are often lined with silk or velvet. Diplomas and certificates These are awarded to the graduates as a symbol of their academic achievement. The diplomas or certificates are typically presented in leather or cardboard holders, which may be embossed with the university's emblem or crest. Ceremonial music Music is often played during the ceremony, with traditional academic songs and hymns being popular choices. pages.content_excerpt: Search Bachelor of Architectural Studies/Bachelor of Architecture – 4/6 years Home / Bachelor of Architectural Studies/Bachelor of Architecture – 4/6 years Minimum entry requirement KCSE minimum aggregate of B- (minus) and C+ (plus) as the minimum grade in cluster Groups of 4 subjects which include: Mathematics, Physics, any subject from Group III (History and Government OR Geography OR Christian Religious Education OR Islamic Religious Education OR Hindu Religious Education); OR 2nd Group II (Biology or Chemistry); OR 2nd Group III OR Group IV (Home Science, or Art and Design or Agriculture or Aviation Technology or Computer Studies); OR Group V (French, German, Arabic, Music, Business Studies) Tuition fees per academic year: Kshs. 266,790/= ( Kenya shillings two hundred sixty six thousand seven hundred ninety only).

pages.content_excerpt: Search Deputy Vice Chancellor Academic Affairs Prof. Robert Kinyua The Academic Division is the largest and controls the core functions of the University; notably planning of academic programmes, preparation of syllabuses, and teaching. The office is also responsible for student’s affairs, including; admissions and records, and welfare.Other functions of the division include; Course regulations, time tables, examinations, certificates and transcripts, graduation, library services, student’s attachment and training of academic staff and appraisals. The Division is headed by Prof. Robert Kinyua who holds a PhD degree in High Energy Physics obtained in 2000 at Osaka University, Japan. He had earlier studied at the University of Nairobi graduating with a masters and undergraduate degrees in Physics in 1993 and 1990 respectively. Prof. Kinyua whose research interests are in high energy physics, radiation physics and renewable energy has widely published with 35 scholarly papers in peer referred journals to his credit.Prior to his appointment, Prof. Kinyua, was the Director, Institute of Energy and Environmental Technology, JKUAT.

pages.content_excerpt: October 29, 2026 October 29, 2026 Corporate Communications JKUAT News Dr. Calvine Ominde the new Dean School of Mathematics and Physical Sciences(SMPS). Dr. Calvine Fundi Ominde, a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Physics at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), has been elected the new Dean of the School of Mathematics and Physical Sciences(SMPS) following a competitive election, ushering in a new chapter in the school’s leadership and academic development. Dr. Ominde emerged victorious in the election, with Dr. Phineas Kiogora finishing as the runner-up. A JKUAT alumnus and former Chair of the Department of Physics, Dr. Ominde succeeds Prof. Anthony Waititu, who has served two terms as dean since October 2022. During the handover ceremony, Prof. Waititu reflected on his tenure and the progress made under his leadership. In his farewell remarks, Prof. Waititu expressed gratitude to members of staff and other stakeholders for their support and cooperation throughout his tenure. This was established during a consultative meeting between the Health Records and Information Management Board of Kenya (HRIM) and the faculty of the College of Health Sciences, JKUAT, March 29, 2023. According to the Chairman, HRIM, Mr. Onesmus Kamau, Continuous education opportunities must be sought to keep their skills and knowledge up-to-date, which will enable them to improve the quality and efficiency of healthcare services provided to patients. The University is at an advanced stage of developing a curriculum for a Bachelor of Biomedical Engineering course, which will soon be offered in the institution’s College of Engineering and Technology, at the School of Mechanical, Manufacturing and Materials Engineering. On Friday March 31, during a stakeholders meeting convened at the University to deliberate on the draft curriculum, the College Principal, Eng. pages.content_excerpt: Doctor of Philosophy in Music Programme Goal The goal of the PhD in Music is to offer rigorous training geared towards enabling students acquire practical skills and knowledge in various aspects of music both as a field of study and profession. This programme aims at providing skills in the area of research methods and techniques, music theory and composition, music performance, music education, production technology, Ethnomusicology, music therapy. Job Placements for the PhD in Music Graduates from this programme are expected to work as music lecturers, curriculum developers, music policy makers, researchers, school administrators and managers, music producers, performing artists and mentors, music producers and composers, music therapists, ethnomusicologists. We also expect graduates of PhD in Music to favourably compete for job opportunities across the globe, as employees of national and international organisations and institutions. headings: Your vote, your choice, choose peace
pages.content_excerpt: Dear Finalists By Hilda Chebet Administration 04 August 2022 Kabarak University has been home to most of you for the past four to five years. You have walked the corridors of this school for so long you could tell where you are just by the trees around you. We congratulate you for the progress you have made this far, from the first year of study until your final year, all the sacrifices failures, and of course, the success that has led you to where you are now, we commend you. We know the journey hasn t been easy, there have been bumps here and there but you adapted to each stage and finally pulled through. We recognize the efforts of all the stakeholders in your journey up to this point. Your parents and guardians, the management, the administration, the chaplaincy, the teaching and non-teaching staff, fellow students and the entire Kabarak community is proud of how far you have come. For the sacrifices they made did indeed bear fruits and you are a true testament to this. As you step out into your next chapter, remember that you are from a world-class university, and you are equipped for whatever you might face in the next chapter. headings: Your vote, your choice, choose peace
pages.content_excerpt: Your vote, your choice, choose peace By Hilda Chebet Administration 04 August 2022 Our country is heading into the elections next week and as we break for the elections on August 9 th , it is important to keep in mind a few things. Our national anthem reminds us to dwell in unity, peace, and liberty. Unity because we are one nation, one people, one identity that is Kenya, we are all Kenyans. Peace because how else do we coexist? how will our children and future generations live if we do not give them peace? How else will we live better together if not peacefully? Liberty because each one of us is given a chance to decide, independence, and freedom to exercise our rights without judgments and interference. On Tuesday, remember that you have the power to make a difference through your vote, the power to give someone a chance to make a difference so go out and make a choice and let others make their choices without interference. Everyone s choice will be different but at the end of the day, we all get a chance to make a choice. pages.content_excerpt: Kabarak University s Master of Oncology Pharmacy Students Complete Clinical Rotation at International Cancer Institute Kabarak University School of Pharmacy 05 March 2025 Hits: 3790 Kabarak University takes immense pride in seeing another group of Master of Oncology Pharmacy students successfully complete their month-long clinical rotation at the International Cancer Institute s (ICI) Clinical Research Unit. This milestone marks yet another step in our commitment to training highly skilled oncology pharmacists equipped to make a difference in cancer treatment and pharmaceutical care. The clinical rotation at ICI provides our students with invaluable hands-on exposure to real-world oncology pharmacy practice. Under the guidance of experienced professionals, they gain practical skills in cancer treatment protocols, pharmaceutical interventions, and patient-centered care crucial competencies in the fight against cancer. Through this immersive training, our students are not just learning; they are actively contributing to oncology care innovations that will enhance cancer treatment outcomes in Africa and beyond. pages.content_excerpt: On March 9th, a delegation from EAST University, led by the Vice Chancellor, visited the Open University of Kenya (OUK) as part of a strategic engagement aimed at exploring opportunities for collaboration in the advancement of Open, Distance and eLearning (ODeL). The team, drawn from the ODeL unit, the Academic Department, and the Information Technology (IT) Department, represented the University’s commitment to building strong partnerships that support innovation and growth in digital education. The visit provided a platform for constructive dialogue between the two institutions on shared priorities in the evolving higher education landscape, particularly in the delivery of flexible and technology-driven learning. Discussions centered on areas of mutual interest such as digital content development, Learning Management System (LMS) infrastructure, student engagement in virtual environments, and frameworks that support quality assurance in online education. The engagement emphasized the importance of collaboration in addressing common challenges and leveraging collective expertise to enhance the accessibility and effectiveness of ODeL programs. pages.content_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to content +254703659032 frontdesk@east.ac.ke | ictsupport@east.ac.ke Buruburu | Kitengela Apply Now Our History The initial roots of KAG-EU can be traced in Tanzania, where the Assemblies of God USA started the Northern Tanganyika Bible School in Arusha in the sixties. Most of our initial KAG Leaders received their ministerial training there. Between September 1975 and 1976, the AG Division of foreign missions decided to shift the Arusha Bible and Theology School from Tanzania to Kenya. The then American AG moderator in Kenya, Rev. Delmer Kingsriter, had always intended for EAST Africa School of Theology (EAST) to serve as a regional school. He approached the Kenya Government for land allocation, and seven and a half acres of land in Buru Buru was granted. In early 1978, Morris Williams, former USA AG General Superintendent, led a group of missionaries and KAG leaders in the groundbreaking ceremony of the new EAST property. EAST opened its Buru Buru campus in September 1979 with only four buildings at various stages of completion. Rev. pages.title: KAG EAST University Opens the Semester with the First Chapel Service of the Year - EAST University
pages.content_excerpt: KAG EAST University joyfully marked the beginning of the January–April semester with its first chapel service of the year, ushering the university community into a new season of spiritual reflection, renewal, and purpose. The semester theme, “A Season of Transformation and Enlargement,” drawn from 2 Peter 1:5–9 and Isaiah 54:1–3 , calls students, faculty, and staff to intentional growth—spiritually, academically, and personally. The scriptures remind us of the importance of cultivating godly character while embracing God’s promise of expansion, fruitfulness, and greater impact. The chapel service provided a meaningful moment for the university community to gather in worship, prayer, and reflection, setting a strong spiritual foundation for the months ahead. It reaffirmed KAG EAST University’s commitment to holistic education that nurtures both academic excellence and spiritual formation. As the semester unfolds, the university looks forward to walking together in this season of transformation and enlargement—strengthening faith, expanding vision, and growing in purpose.

We believe true learning inspires action, compassion, and innovation that uplift not just individuals, but entire communities. Through our diverse programs, students are equipped with both academic knowledge and practical experience that prepare them to respond to real-world challenges. From community outreach to leadership development, every part of our training is designed to build purpose-driven graduates who make a difference wherever they go. Our vision is to raise leaders who understand that success is not measured only by personal achievement, but by the positive impact one leaves in society. As we continue to grow, we remain committed to nurturing a generation of thinkers, creators, and change-makers who serve with integrity, skill, and heart. Transforming minds. Empowering communities. Shaping the future one student at a time.
