pages.title: Keep Showing Up, Even on the Tough Days - EAST University
pages.content_excerpt: Campus life isn’t always smooth. There are weeks when assignments pile up, Wi-Fi disappears when you need it most, and motivation feels like a myth. But growth doesn’t happen on perfect days — it happens when you keep showing up despite the noise. The student who studies when it’s hard, the lecturer who keeps mentoring even when few listen, the staff member who gives excellence quietly — that’s what builds the true spirit of a university. Small steps done faithfully every day create the future everyone will one day admire. Keep at it. Keep believing. Greatness grows in consistency. — East University

pages.title: First-Year Orientation Day Three: Navigating ICT, Academic Systems and University Life - Kenya Highlands University Kericho
pages.content_excerpt: The First-Year Students’ Orientation Programme at Kenya Highlands University continued successfully on Day Three, with students receiving practical and essential information aimed at helping them make a smooth transition into university life and confidently navigate their academic journey. The day focused on equipping students with knowledge of the University’s ICT services, with particular emphasis on academic ICT services, the ERP Portal and Online and Distance e-Learning (ODeL) . pages.content_excerpt: Last Friday, August 22nd, 2025, marked a historic milestone as Kenya Methodist University (KeMU) celebrated its very first Founders Day. It was a day to pause, reflect, and honour the visionary men and women who laid the foundation for our great university and nurtured the dream that has brought us to where we are today. A Vision Rooted in Methodist Values Methodist education has always aimed for holistic development – combining academic excellence with strong moral values, discipline, and a heart for service to others. The Methodist Church envisioned establishing a university that would bring these transformative principles to our society, and that vision became the seed from which KeMU grew. pages.title: KeMU Pharmacy Students Shine at the 2026 World Pharmacy Day Intervarsity Olympiad - Kenya Methodist University
pages.content_excerpt: Kenya Methodist University (KeMU) Pharmacy students have once again demonstrated excellence after emerging Overall Second Best University out of nine universities at the 2026 World Pharmacy Day Intervarsity Olympiad. Five trophies for KeMU Overall ranking: 2nd position out of 9 universities Preclinical skills: 1st position Clinical skills: 1st position General pharmacy quiz: 1st position Industrial skills: 2nd position This remarkable achievement marks four consecutive years of outstanding performance at the World Pharmacy Day Intervarsity Olympiad, reflecting the excellence, dedication and practical competence of KeMU Pharmacy students. Competing against eight other pharmacy schools from across the country, the KeMU team delivered an outstanding performance. Congratulations to our Pharmacy students and the entire Pharmacy Department for flying the KeMU flag high.

pages.content_excerpt: Kenya Methodist University (KeMU), Tuesday, 16th September 2025, held the Matriculation Ceremony for the September 2025 intake of fresh men and women at the Main Campus, Meru. The ceremony marked an important milestone in the life of our new students as they officially joined the KeMU academic community, committing themselves to a journey of faith, purpose and excellence. Prayer and Dedication In a moment of prayer and reflection, the new students gathered in the chapel, dedicating their academic journey to God. The University Chaplain, Rev. Dr. Jeniffer Lairang’i, led a prayer, committing their studies to the Lord, drawing inspiration from Scripture: “Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and He will establish your plans.” – Proverbs 16:3 (NIV) The Vice Chancellor, Rev. Prof. John Kobia Ataya, PhD, who was also the chief speaker of the day, warmly welcomed the new students, describing the day as the beginning of a transformative journey. He encouraged them to embrace new beginnings, approach the new norm with an open mind, remain focused and leave a lasting mark. pages.content_excerpt: +254 20 870 3000/4000 info@ku.ac.ke Nairobi, Kenya Student Portal Staff Portal Apply Online About Kenyatta University Over four decades of academic excellence, research and nation-building Home About KU History & Background Kenyatta University (KU) was established as a constituent college of the University of Nairobi in 1970, and was granted its own charter in 1985. Named after Kenya's founding father, Mzee Jomo Kenyatta, the university has grown from a small teacher training college into one of East Africa's largest and most respected institutions of higher learning. From its humble beginnings with a few hundred students, KU today enrolls over 70,000 students across undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes. The university operates multiple campuses across Kenya, with the main campus located in Kahawa, Nairobi County. Over the decades, KU has built a strong reputation for teacher education, science and technology, public health, law, and business studies, producing graduates who are contributing meaningfully to Kenya's development and beyond. 1970 Founded as Constituent College 1985 Granted Full University Charter 55+ Years of Academic Excellence Vision & Mission Our Vis

pages.content_excerpt: International Women’s Day at MNUC The 2024 International Women’s Day celebrations were held by MNUC Members of Management, students and staff on Friday 8th March, 2024 in the MNUC. The celebrations culminated with a presenation aligned to the this year’s theme”Invest in Women, Accelerate Progress” Dr. Ruth Mbugua -Dean, School of Nursing who was the keynote speaker delivered a speech on gender equality which served as the pinnacle of the event. With her unparalleled expertise and passion, she illuminated the audience with insights and perspectives that resonated deeply with the theme. Her words were not merely informative but transformative, igniting a renewed commitment to advancing gender equality. Dr. Ruth’s presence and message encapsulated the spirit of the event, inspiring attendees to advocate for inclusivity and empowerment in all aspects of society. The attendees were also sensitized on the MNUC Sexual and Gender-Based Violence Policy by the Gender Focal Person, Ms. Josephine Nkangi Dr. Ruth Mbugua -Dean school of Health Sciences -Key note speaker addressing the participants Participants during the celebrations Isaac Kuria 2024-03-15T07:35:41+00:00

pages.content_excerpt: Mutomo landowners to get millions in Mama Ngina University expansion plan In Summary • The land was acquired by the government to pave way for the expansion of Mama Ngina University. • The university was constructed in 2019 on 10.3 acres and the management has been seeking 40 acres for expansion. Each of the 191 property owners will receive a minimum of Sh10 million for their quarter-acre plots A dispute over the compensation of land to allow for the expansion of Mama Ngina University in Mutomo village, Gatundu, in Kiambu has been resolved. In the deal brokered by the National Land Commission, each of the 191 property owners will receive a minimum of Sh10 million for their quarter-acre plots. The highest amount to be paid per plot is Sh35 million. The land was acquired by the government to pave way for the expansion of Mama Ngina University. The university was constructed in 2019 on 10.3 acres and the management has been seeking 40 acres for expansion. NLC valuer and project team leader Doricah Buyaki said the compensation cash will vary depending on developments in the property. headings: Kibabii University Team Concludes African AI Upskilling Programme Train-the-Trainer Workshop in Nairobi
pages.content_excerpt: Skip to content Kibabii University Team Concludes African AI Upskilling Programme Train-the-Trainer Workshop in Nairobi October 28, 2026 Kibabii University AI Upskilling Champions attended a Train-the-Trainer (TtT) workshop held from 19 to 23 October 2026 under the African AI Upskilling Programme, delivered by the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) in collaboration with Google DeepMind. The intensive five-day workshop, hosted at the United States International University–Africa (USIU-Africa) in Nairobi, brought together Kibabii University’s AI Champions and Teaching Assistants alongside participants from the University of Embu and Zetech University. The training focused on equipping participants with practical knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence, machine learning and AI research foundations, while preparing them to facilitate AI learning and champion the adoption of AI technologies within their respective institutions. pages.title: About Us
pages.content_excerpt: Facebook Instagram Twitter YouTube LinkedIn Whatsapp - +254728499650 Welcome to Kirinyaga University Our History About Kirinyaga university Kirinyaga University (KyU) is located approximately 115 Km North East of Nairobi on Sagana - Embu - Highway. It is the successor to Kirinyaga Technical Institute which was conceived by the people of Kirinyaga way back in 1971 when the former head of state His Excellency the President, Hon. Daniel Arap Moi C.G.H., M.P. (then Vice-president) launched the Harambee Fund Raising Drive at the request of Kirinyaga people. Kirinyaga County Council set aside 200 acres of land for the institute at Kutus and 50 more acres were also acquired at Kangaita area on the slopes of Mt. Kenya. The Institute opened doors to the first students on 2nd March 1977 when 72 students were enrolled, 48 of these students were admitted in the building and construction department while the remaining 24 were enrolled in the clothing and textile technology department. New training programmes were introduced in plumbing and Electrical installation in the early and mid-eighties respectively. These programs are designed to advance research skills, generate and globally disseminate new knowledge and enhance professional competence and skills application in the various disciplines. Postgraduate Diploma programs are designed to advance knowledge, technical skills, aptitude and competence in the respective disciplines. Master degree programs aim at advancing knowledge and development of specialized technical skills, coupled with advanced research skills in the respective area of specialization. pages.content_excerpt: × Main Menu Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Medicine – Kirinyaga University Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Medicine – Kirinyaga University Kirinyaga University has successfully mounted a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Medicine, a strategic advancement that strengthens the University’s role in postgraduate medical education, specialized clinical research, and health innovation. The programme is designed to train senior clinicians, medical researchers, and academic leaders capable of generating high-quality scientific evidence to improve healthcare delivery and outcomes. The PhD in Clinical Medicine places strong emphasis on independent, original, and impactful research that addresses pressing national and global health challenges. Candidates are rigorously trained in advanced research methodologies, biostatistics, clinical epidemiology, medical ethics, and translational research, ensuring the production of graduates who can integrate scientific discovery into clinical practice and health policy formulation. pages.content_excerpt: Prof. Nathan Oyaro, DSc Deputy Vice Chancellor (AP&F) Prof. Nathan Oyaro, DSc Deputy Vice Chancellor (AP&F) Professor Nathan Oyaro is a Professor of Atmospheric and Environmental Chemistry. With over 30 years of experience in higher education, he has established himself as a distinguished scholar, researcher, and academic leader in environmental and analytical chemistry. He holds a Doctor of Science (DSc) in Physical Chemistry (Atmospheric Chemistry) from the University of Oslo, Norway, and MSc and BSc degrees from Kenyatta University. Throughout his academic career, he has served in several senior leadership positions, including Dean of the School of Science, Director of Research, and Head of academic and governance committees, contributing significantly to institutional development and research excellence. Professor Oyaro's research focuses on atmospheric chemistry, environmental pollution, climate change, water quality, phytoremediation, renewable energy, and sustainable environmental technologies. He has secured competitive national and international research funding, led multidisciplinary research collaborations, and published extensively in peer-reviewed scientific journals.

pages.content_excerpt: There are two categories of students at the Kisii university: Government Sponsored Students Self Sponsored Students Application process for Government Sponsored Students The Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) is the state corporation that coordinates the placement of Government-Sponsored Students to Kenyan universities and colleges. KUCCPS undertakes the selection of undergraduate students for admission to higher learning institutions for Government sponsorship. KUCCPS placement criteria a) Only candidates who apply for placement will be considered for placement in the respective programmes applied b) Candidates must meet the minimum admission requirement approved by the respective regulating authority to be considered for placement c) Placement shall be on merit d) An affirmative action criteria approved by the Placement Service shall be applied for the marginalized and disadvantaged applicants. e) Applicants who will not manage to be placed in the preferred programmes may be requested to re-apply for placement consideration into programmes which may not satisfied the number required. Kisii University College was founded in 1965 as a Primary Teachers Training College on a 61 acre land that was donated by the County Council of Gusii. The college continued up to 1983 when it was upgraded to a Secondary Teachers College to offer Diploma programmes. The Government of Kenya mandated Egerton University to take over the College as its campus in 1994. In 1999, the Faculty of Commerce established Bachelor of Business and Management as its first degree program within the campus to run alongside Post Graduate Diploma in Education (PGDE), which was phased out in the year 2001. On 23rd August 2007, Kisii University College was established through a Government Legal Notice No.163 of 2007 as a constituent College of Egerton University. On 6th February 2013, Former President Mwai Kibaki through Legal Notice No 225 granted Kisii University Charter in accordance to the Universities Act 2012 How To Apply For more information contact +254720875082

pages.content_excerpt: Introduction A Bachelor of Science in Physics of Kisii University is an undergraduate academic degree program that focuses on the study of the fundamental principles governing the behavior of matter and energy in the universe. Physics is a branch of science that seeks to understand the natural world at its most fundamental level and is a cornerstone of modern scientific research and technological development. During a Bachelor of Science in Physics program, students typically engage in a combination of theoretical and practical coursework. They study topics such as classical mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics, relativity, optics, and more. The program often includes laboratory work, where students gain hands-on experience conducting experiments and verifying theoretical concepts. Here are some key aspects of a Bachelor of Science in Physics program: Core Concepts: Students develop a strong foundation in the principles of physics, exploring how matter and energy interact and the mathematical models used to describe these interactions. pages.content_excerpt: Introduction World,s energy demand has continued to grow over the past half century owing to high increase in population and industrial advancement. About 80% percent of this energy comes from none renewable energy sources such as oil, coal and natural gases. Over years, these energy sources will be depleted resulting in energy crisis. It is from this perspective that the world energy today is moving in the direction of renewable energy sources such as solar energy, geothermal energy, wind energy, Biomass energy and hydro energy. For maximum extraction, distribution and proper utilization of this energy, scientist with vast knowledge in this area required. It is for this reason that Bachelor of Science in Renewable Energy of Kisii University was developed. The course is aimed at equipping the graduates with high theoretical and technical skills to allow them work competently in various renewable energy firms as technicians, analysts, consultants among other positions within these firms. pages.content_excerpt: ACADEMICS DIRECTORATE Message from the Registrar Academic Affairs Cs John N. Ngigi serves as the Registrar Academic Affairs at Koitaleel Samoei University College. The Office of the Registrar, Academic Affairs is responsible for the effective management of all academic operations. This includes student admissions, maintenance of student records, implementation of academic policies, coordination of examinations, issuance of transcripts and certificates, and oversight of curriculum delivery. The office acts as the official custodian of student academic data and ensures strict adherence to university academic regulations. Cs Ngigi holds a Master’s degree in Education Administration and a Bachelor’s degree in Education (Arts), both from the University of Nairobi. He is a Certified Public Secretary, an accredited Governance Auditor, and a member of the Institute of Certified Public Secretaries of Kenya. He has also undertaken advanced training in management, including the Strategic Leadership Development Programme (SLDP). With over a decade of progressive experience in university administration, Cs Ngigi brings deep expertise to his role. Prior to his appointment as Registrar Academic A

A seasoned scholar, researcher, mentor, coach, and transformative leader, Prof. Guyo brings extensive experience in learning and development, people empowerment, and progressive human capital development. He takes over from Prof. John Kanjogu , who assumes the substantive position of the Director Research Human Rights and Gender. He served diligently in an acting capacity since January 2025. During the ceremony, Prof. Kanjogu thanked the University Council for the trust bestowed upon him and expressed appreciation to the University Management and staff within the Academic Division for their support during his tenure. pages.title: Prof. Wendo Nabea Leads Inaugural School Seminar at Laikipia University | Laikipia University
headings: Prof. Wendo Nabea Leads Inaugural School Seminar at Laikipia University
pages.content_excerpt: The School of Humanities and Development Studies at Laikipia University marked an important academic milestone on 16th September 2026 with its first seminar presentation , held at Mandela Hall. The seminar was delivered by Prof. Wendo Nabea , a distinguished member of the University’s academic staff, on the topic “From Utubora to Utuume: Towards a Theory of Utuume through Shaaban Robert’s Utubora Mkulima.” The presentation provided an engaging platform for scholarly reflection, exchange of ideas and intellectual discussion among members of the University community. As the first seminar of its kind within the School, the event represents an encouraging step towards nurturing a stronger culture of academic dialogue and knowledge sharing. The University looks forward to more such engagements that provide opportunities for its scholars to share their work, inspire new thinking and contribute to the advancement of knowledge. He holds a PhD in Botany (Plant Pathology) from Maseno University, a Master of Science in Botany (Plant Pathology), and a Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Education and Extension from Egerton University. Maina Head Health Services Department The University Health Services Department is one of the Departments under the Administration and Finance division of the university. The Health facility is registered as “Maasai Mara University Health Centre” with the Medical Practitioners and Dentists Board , affiliate sections (Pharmacy and Laboratory) registered with relevant Boards. Its main function is to provide quality health care through curative, preventive, supportive and psychological care to students’ fraternity, staff and their dependents, disciplined forces and civil servants through National Hospital Insurance Fund policy as an income-generating facility. At the MMARAU Health Center, we strive to meet all the University communities medical needs. We enjoy the experience of well-staffed medical personnel. As a body of certified professionals, we strive to live up to our professional code of conduct. We treat all the patient’s information with the utmost confidentiality. This approach combines synergies from Open and Distance Learning (ODL) and E-Learning raising the standards of teaching and learning and providing opportunities for lifelong learning. The Center is also supporting implementation of E-Learning through its e-academy. The e-academy is increase access to education and promoting inclusivity in education. pages.content_excerpt: Introduction to Agroecological and Integrated Aqua-Agriculture Course Basic article Mar 18, 2026 Image Welcome to Maseno University platform for an online course on agroecology. This course is designed as a flexible self-study programme that allows participants to learn at their own pace while gaining essential knowledge on sustainable agricultural systems and integrated food production approaches. The course introduces the scientific foundations and practical applications of agroecology, emphasizing environmentally sound farming practices that enhance productivity, strengthen resilience, and conserve natural resources. Learners explore key concepts such as biodiversity conservation, soil fertility management, nutrient recycling, ecological pest regulation, and climate-resilient farming systems that support long-term sustainability. This online learning platform is developed under the PrAEctiCe Project, an initiative funded by the European Union and implemented by Maseno University in collaboration with diverse international partners. pages.content_excerpt: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology has today, 27 th October, 2026, elected Deans to lead various Schools for a three-year term. In a highly competitive race, candidates vying for Deanship demonstrated political prowess while maintaining academic decorum expected of leaders of their caliber. Today’s elections were preceded by a two-week campaign period and the ‘ Big Debate ’, which saw candidates present their manifestos to prospective voters. Prof. Elizabeth Omukunda won the coveted position of Dean for the School of Natural Sciences (SONAS); Dr. Paul Ogenga secured the School of Education (SEDU); Dr. Micah Mukolwe was elected to the School of Engineering and Built Environment (SEBE); and Dr. Evans Raballah took the helm at the School of Public Health, Biomedical Sciences and Technology (SPHB&T). Meanwhile, three (3) positions were secured unopposed, namely: Prof. Vitalis Ogemah for the School of Agriculture, Veterinary Sciences and Technology (SAVET), Dr. Dishon Wanjere for the School of Business and Economics (SOBE), and Dr. Gregory Sakwa for the School of Nursing, Midwifery and Paramedical Sciences (SONMAPS). pages.content_excerpt: About the programme The Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) programme has been granted provisional accreditation by the Medical Practitioners and Dentists Board. The School will train doctors and will impart appropriate theoretical, research and practical knowledge, skills and attitudes that are responsive to the health needs of the Kenyan society. The programme covers pre-clinical which include; Human Anatomy, Medical Physiology, Medical Biochemistry, Medical Microbiology and Parasitology, Behavioural Sciences and Ethics, Community Health, Pathology and clinical areas; Anesthesia, Internal Medicine, Surgery, Reproductive Health, Mental Health, Child Health and Paediatrics, Orthopedic Surgery Vision of the programme To be a role model of excellence in science and technology, education and training in Africa. Mission of the programme To contribute to the society by provision of accessible and innovative quality medical education that promotes excellence in scholarship, research and equitable service to the communities. pages.content_excerpt: Mount Kenya University established the Department of Education following the grant of Letter of Interim Authority by the then Commission of Higher Education in 2008. Due to the need to facilitate upgrading of competences and skills by primary and secondary schools teachers, the school started offering school-based programmes in 2009. In 2010 the department of Education was upgraded into the School of Education with; the Department of Education Management and Department of Early Childhood. Also due to the need to expand access to the University programmes, virtual-based learning was introduced in 2010. In 2015, the departments in the School of Education were increased to four. Following the need assessment survey which was conducted in 2016 and whose findings indicated some shortcomings about school-based education programmes, the programmes were rebranded, “Distance and Institution-Based Learning” housed in a full Directorate of Distance and Institution-Based Learning. pages.content_excerpt: Nursing is one of the most exciting professions today, as new health care technology is creating opportunities for nurses. More and more aspects of the profession are electronic: Test results, X-rays, blood work, and ordering medication. New technologies like mobile devices, electronic medical records, computing, and teleconferencing invite nurses to be digitally ambitious. Nursing encompasses autonomous and collaborative care of individuals, families, groups and communities, sick or well and in all settings. With the right skills and knowledge, the next generation of nurses can make a bigger difference. The concept of best practice in nursing is an important one. New knowledge based on nursing and related interdisciplinary research is rapidly expanding. Provision of high quality care depends on translating research-based knowledge into real-life nursing practice. This practice is encouraged a lot at Mount Kenya University, School of nursing The school is organized in departments as follows: midwifery, community health nursing, medical surgical nursing & Nursing education, leadership management and research . pages.content_excerpt: Rationale for the programme Needs assessment / situation analysis Development of the original curriculum arose from need for academic progression by Diploma in Nutrition and Dietetics graduates. The need to review this curriculum arose from the need to align it with the requirements of the regulatory body (The Kenya Nutritionists and Dieticians Institute). Needs assessment was done in consultation with the stakeholders and the university curriculum review committee. The stakeholders included; Nutrition and Dietetics Students, Ministry of Health, The Kenya Nutritionists and Dieticians Institute, Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development, NGO representatives, Kenya National Examinations Council, representatives from other higher education institutions, this led to a review of the course content and duration of study. Justification for the need of the programme Right to good nutrition is a human right entrenched in the Kenyan constitution. The high incidence and prevalence of preventable nutrition related diseases, the emergence of new diseases and food insecurity indicates that not all Kenyans enjoy this right. pages.content_excerpt: Rationale for the programme The high incidence and prevalence of preventable diseases, the emergence of new diseases, food insecurity and the need for proper Nutrition, places a heavy demand on the training institutions offering nutrition related courses. Advances in I.C.T call for a need to improve training Curriculum to be relevant to today’s market and to improve on operational research in the endeavour to meet Kenyan developmental goals as well as solve malnutrition problems in Kenya and Africa as a region. Nutrition activities are being incorporated in development programmes and planners are using nutrition outcomes such as improved nutritional status to evaluate the impact of these programmes. With co-operation between local communities, NGO’s and government, the lives of our people can be improved, healthy growth and development and greater productivity can be achieved through good nutrition. Lack of access to good education and correct information can hamper this. Without information accessible from research and education programmes, the awareness, skills and behaviour needed to combat malnutrition cannot be attained. pages.content_excerpt: Mount Kenya University School of Social Sciences comprises the departments of Psychology, Humanities and Languages; Social and Development Studies; Journalism and Mass Communication; and Institute of Security Studies, Justice and Ethics. The departments offer postgraduate, undergraduate, diploma and certificate courses in various disciplines such as psychology, international relations, diplomacy, development studies, journalism and media studies, diplomacy, governance, security studies and criminology, peace studies and public administration. We cultivate the ability of students to think critically, conduct research and draw logical conclusion while at the same time expressing their thoughts effectively, with the overall intention of providing them with learning experiences to position them to serve and function in a dynamic global environment.

pages.content_excerpt: Welcome to the School of Pure and Applied Sciences The School of Pure and Applied Sciences (SPAS) forms one of the 15 schools of Mount Kenya University and has a student population approximately 1100. The School targets at providing Pure and Applied Sciences as a major vehicle for attaining and sustaining industrial development of Kenya which is consistent with the vision 2030 Economic Pillar. In line with the university’s vision and mission, the School is committed to raise the skill competencies, and the numbers required to make Kenya a competitive industrialized nation by developing centers of excellence in the training of, technicians, para-veterinarians, biotechnologists, actuarial scientists, ecologists, entomologists, molecular biologists, chemists, statisticians, and agriculturalists among others. Our programs offer high-level education and research training on basic and applied sciences in cooperation with highly qualified faculty staff, aiming to develop students into researchers and, innovators as well as highly specialized professionals with broad vision, excellent research skills, and ability to adapt them to rapidly changing demands in line with Kenya’s vision 2030 go

pages.course_name: MMU considers launching degree courses in Education - Multimedia University of Kenya
pages.content_excerpt: Multimedia University of Kenya (MMU), has initiated a strategic effort to explore the possibility of launching degree programmes in Education. The university has set up an ad hoc committee to engage with key stakeholders and benchmark with leading institutions in the education sector. The ad hoc committee, led by Prof. Iyaya Wanjala has already visited Teachers Service Commission (TSC), Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD), Technical and Vocational Education Training Authority (TVETA), among other key education training institutions for benchmarking initiatives. According of Prof. Iyaya, the committee’s primary objective is to assess resources needed to establish Faculty of Education, and to guide in development of the corresponding education programs. He also noted that MMU plans to leverage its established strengths in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) and Media Technology by producing highly competent teachers in the mentioned areas. MMU Education ad hoc committee with KICD Director Prof. Charles O. Ong’ondo (fourth right) and other senior KICD staff during a benchmarking exercise on Wednesday, July 24, 2024. pages.content_excerpt: THE FUTURE OF MMU Multimedia University of Kenya’s vision is in sync with Kenya Vision 2030. As an Information age institution MMU shall play a pivotal role in the ICT initiatives in terms of providing qualified personnel for the fulfillment of the vision. The University will unveil more training programmes by the faculties and schools both at undergraduate and post graduate levels. These courses will be offered in consultation with market leaders so as to address the quality and relevance. Being an ICT Centre of Excellence, the university looks forward to hosting the Open University of Kenya and the establishment of the Kenya Advanced Institute of Science and Technology by the Korean Government. The university is always open to enhancing its opportunities, expanding its capacity and signing more partnerships/ MOUs which benefit the University and community. pages.title: PhD in Development Studies
pages.content_excerpt: Overview Admission Requirements Fees and Funding Exam Regulation and Grading Overview The PhD in Development Studies at Murang'a University is designed to equip students with advanced knowledge and research skills in the field of development. The program focuses on critical issues such as poverty alleviation, sustainable development, and social justice. It prepares graduates for careers in academia, research institutions, government, and non-governmental organizations. Admission Requirements To be eligible for admission to the PhD in Development Studies, applicants must meet the following criteria: A Master's degree in Development Studies or a related field from Murang'a University or any other institution recognized by the Commission for University Education. A strong academic record with a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. Submission of a research proposal outlining the intended area of study and methodology. Two letters of recommendation from academic or professional referees. A personal statement detailing the applicant's motivation for pursuing the PhD and career aspirations. Students will engage in rigorous academic research and practical applications that prepare them for leadership roles in academia, industry, and government. Omwenga, has been honored with the Transformational Leadership Award in Digital Higher Education & Institutional Transformation. Presented by the AC-TLA Technical Working Committee under Arise Circle Africa and Arise Circle Kenya, this prestigious international recognition celebrates Prof. Omwenga’s visionary leadership as an educational executive, ICT innovator, scholar, and researcher. His work has significantly advanced digital learning, strengthened university systems, and accelerated inclusive, technology-driven higher education. Under his leadership, the Open University of Kenya has championed accessible, future-focused learning pathways, positioning the institution on the global map of digital higher education. His contributions align with Kenya’s Vision 2030, Africa’s Agenda 2063, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, notably SDGs 4, 5, 8, and 9. pages.content_excerpt: Skip to main content Post Graduate Diploma in Education Postgraduate Diploma in Education Duration: 1 Year Start Date: Cost: KES 110,000 per year Mode of Delivery: Online Application Due: Open Fee Structure and Payment APPLY NOW Overview The Post Graduate Diploma in Education (PGDE) offers a flexible and high-quality education tailored for aspiring educators. The programme's goal is to equip learners with knowledge, skills and competencies for effective teaching and educational management. pages.content_excerpt: Image Academic Collaboration: Open University of Kenya and Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore Latest News / February 29, 2024 Submitted by webadmin on February 29, 2024 On February 28, 2024, the Vice Chancellor of the Open University of Kenya Prof. Elijah Omwenga, alongside the University management, welcomed Prof. Mario Molteni, Professor of Corporate Strategy at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Milan . Prof. Molteni also serves as the Rector's Delegate for Business Relations, CEO of E4Impact Foundation , and President of ALTIS Advisory. The meeting took place at the offices of the Open University of Kenya situated in KONZA Technopolis City. During the meeting, representatives from both institutions reached several agreements. They decided to collaborate on various initiatives, notably the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the Open University of Kenya and the Catholic University of Milan. Additionally, they agreed to co-host certain degree programs, including an MBA in Entrepreneurship. pages.content_excerpt: Skip to main content FAQs Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. What are the minimum admission requirements for undergraduate programs at the Open University of Kenya? The minimum requirements include a mean grade of C+ and above at KCSE (Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education) or its equivalent. Alternatively, applicants with diplomas, professional qualifications, or other qualifications recognized by the Senate are eligible. 2. Can I apply with a KCSE certificate alone, or do I need additional qualifications? While a KCSE certificate is accepted, you may also need to provide a certificate of completion for foundation or bridging courses from recognized institutions to meet the eligibility criteria. 3. Is work experience considered for admission? Yes, work experience can be considered for admission. You can provide evidence of two years of work experience in a relevant field as part of your application. 4. Are there specific short courses I need to complete for admission? pages.content_excerpt: Skip to main content The Governing Council Chair of Council Professor Ezra Maritim Prof Ezra Maritim earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from University of Nairobi in 1973. Upon graduation that year, he was awarded University of Nairobi staff development scholarship under the sponsorship of the Carnegie Foundation of New York for postgraduate studies at Harvard University and subsequently earned Master of Education and Doctor of Education degrees from Harvard University in 1975 and 1979, respectively. Prof Maritim spent many years at Kenyatta University both as a teacher and administrator. He served as University Secretary and Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Finance, Planning, and Development & Administration). Between 1983 and 1990 he was seconded to serve as a Deputy Secretary, Kenya National Examinations Council. Other administrative positions he has held in higher education landscape include being a Deputy Coordinator, World Bank supported University Investment Project; Deputy Secretary, Commission for Higher Education and the Vice-Chancellor, Egerton University. pages.title: History of OUK | Open University of Kenya
pages.content_excerpt: Skip to main content History of OUK History of the Open University Since gaining independence in 1963, Kenya has recognized the need for reforms in education to address issues such as access, equity, quality, and relevance. These reforms have included increasing the number of schools, colleges, and universities through public and private participation, implementing quota systems and gender considerations in admissions, providing teacher training and retraining, improving infrastructure to support teaching and learning, and reforming the curriculum. Public participation, through the establishment of Education Commissions and Task Forces, has played a role in identifying the challenges facing the education sector. However, the mainstreaming of distance learning, as a means to increase access to higher education, has been underdeveloped and underfunded in Kenya, despite the establishment of the African Virtual University in 1997.The need for increased access to higher education has been recognized for decades in Kenya, with the government investing significantly in higher education for training and research. pages.content_excerpt: Skip to main content ICT Professional Certification ICT Professional Certification The Open University of Kenya (OUK), in collaboration with Huawei, has launched a Huawei ICT Academy on campus. This initiative aims to equip students with cutting-edge ICT skills—including Artificial Intelligence—culminating in dual professional certification from OUK and Huawei. The Huawei Certified ICT Associate – Artificial Intelligence (HCIA-AI) course offers a comprehensive learning pathway, covering foundational AI concepts, hands-on practical labs, exposure to Huawei’s robust ecosystem, and globally recognized certification—all delivered by OUK-certified trainers. Learners will gain proficiency in machine learning and deep learning algorithms for designing and developing AI products and solutions. This course responds to the growing demand for AI professionals across industries in Kenya and globally. With AI technologies now driving innovation in sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, finance, education, and transportation, there is a pressing need for skilled individuals who can understand, develop, and apply AI solutions. This guide is suitable for individuals at all levels of information searching and usage. The Project is a five-year flagship Government investment aimed at transforming Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education across public universities. Through targeted investments in infrastructure, modern equipment, academic capacity, research and governance systems, the Project seeks to ensure that universities are fully prepared to receive learners transitioning from the Competency-Based Education (CBE) pathway, while also producing graduates equipped with relevant skills, strong innovation capacity and global competitiveness. Through VotersWall, a cutting-edge digital voting system, OUK has set a new benchmark for secure, transparent and efficient electoral processes in learning institutions across Kenya. Developed by a student of Innovation At the core of this success was cybersecurity, a key component in safeguarding voter data and maintaining election integrity. Developed by Innocent Kiboto, a student of the Bachelor of Science in Cyber Security and Digital Forensics at OUK, the system employs end-to-end encryption, multi-factor authentication and real-time monitoring to prevent tampering and unauthorized access. These robust security measures fostered trust among students, administrators and election stakeholders, positioning VotersWall as a game-changer in digital elections. The Workshop brought together academic experts from over thirty universities, institutions and industry players to collaboratively develop and refine first, second, and third-year course content across various academic programmes. A workshop by Rongo University, department of Communication, Journalism and Media Studies and
African Health Solution Journalism Initiative (AHSJI)

A workshop by Rongo University, department of Communication, Journalism and Media Studies and
African Health Solution Journalism Initiative (AHSJI) At the workshop, AHSJI was represented by the Project Lead, Daniel Otunge and Media Consultant, David Aduda. AHSJI seeks to introduce Solution Journalism to African academies so as to transform the reporting of health and development issues. Solution Journalism (SOJO) strives to help journalists focus on proven solutions to problems rather than just focusing on the problems. Through soJO, the role of the media also evolves from that of a watch dog to societal guide dogs. The outcome of the workshop is a collaboration between Rongo University, department of Communication, Journalism and Media Studies and African Health Solution Journalism Initiative through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). The following will be achieved through the collaboration:
i. Training of trainers
i. Internship and fellowship for Rongo University Students
ii. Resource mobilization through joint Proposal Writing.
iv. Curriculum Development.

pages.content_excerpt: Audit INTERNAL AUDIT DEPARTMENT Introduction The internal audit department aims to provide an independent objective assurance and consulting activity designed to add value and improve the university’s operations. It helps the university to realize its objectives by bringing a systematic approach to evaluate and improve the effectiveness of controls, risk management and the governance processes. The university supports Internal Audit as an independent appraisal function to examine and evaluate activities at the University as a service to management and the Council. Core Functions Conducting audits on identified risk areas and specific functions to ascertain the effectiveness and efficiency of operations. Ensuring that the University complies with statutory obligations, plans, policies and procedures. Ensuring that the University assets are accounted for and safeguarded from loss or pilferage. Evaluating and providing recommendations to improve operating efficiency and internal controls, risk management and governance. John Kipngetich Mosonik, CBS, EBS, is a distinguished technocrat with 35 years of executive leadership across public and private sectors, spanning telecommunications engineering, infrastructure, energy, and strategic governance. He is a Fellow of the Institution of Engineers of Kenya (FIEK) and registered with the Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK). He holds a DBA in Strategic Leadership (Northcentral University, USA), a PhD in Strategic Management (Moi University, Kenya), and advanced postgraduate degrees in Digital Transformation, Finance, Strategic Focus, and Business Administration, alongside a BSc in Electrical Engineering (Telecommunications, University of Nairobi). His key achievements include spearheading 6,000 km of rural roads across 47 Kenyan counties, pioneering telecom and oil and gas projects, and shaping national industrialization policies. pages.content_excerpt: History Welcome to Rongo University (RU) A Prestigious Institution with a Rich History Explore Our Journey Welcome to Rongo University (RU) A Prestigious Institution with a Rich History of Growth, Innovation and Academic Excellence Our Journey Welcome to Rongo University (RU) , a prestigious institution with a rich history dating back to the early 1970s. Discover the remarkable journey of our University from its humble beginnings as Kitere Technical School to its present status as a fully-fledged public university committed to excellence in teaching, research, innovation and community service. 1970s Humble Beginnings Established in the early 1970s as Kitere Technical School , the institution was founded by the local community to serve as a craft apprenticeship training centre. It provided practical technical skills that empowered young people within the South Nyanza region. During the 1980s, demand for technical and vocational education increased significantly. Prof. Jacob Kibor, PhD Welcome to Scott Christian University. Welcome to Scott Christian University, a place where faith, knowledge, and character are nurtured to shape transformative leaders for our society. As Chancellor, I am honored to be part of an institution deeply committed to academic excellence, spiritual growth, and service to humanity. At Scott Christian University, we believe education goes beyond the classroom. We strive to cultivate integrity, critical thinking, and a strong moral foundation in every student, preparing them to make meaningful contributions in their professions and communities. Our dedicated faculty and staff work tirelessly to provide a supportive and enriching environment where each student can thrive. I invite you to join our vibrant community and be part of a legacy that is grounded in Christian values and driven by a vision for a better future. Together, we can inspire change, empower lives, and build a generation of leaders who will make a lasting impact.

From a modest theological college in Machakos to a fully chartered university, our purpose has never changed: Scott Christian University remains committed to nurturing graduates who are intellectually competent, ethically grounded, professionally equipped, and purposefully prepared to transform the Church, the marketplace, and society through servant leadership and innovation. Vice Chancellor Rev. Prof. Jonathan Mwania Welcome to Scott Christian University, a community where faith and scholarship meet. It is my privilege to lead an institution that has, since 1962, formed generations of graduates for service in church, society and the marketplace. headings: Your application to SCU, step by step.

What it costs · how we help.
Up to 50% off tuition for qualifying students.
pages.content_excerpt: +254 713 745 404 | +254 706 381 396 info@scott.ac.ke Staff Portal Student Portal Library KUCCPS Application → Home / Admissions September 2026 intake · Open Your application to SCU, step by step. Thank you for your interest in Scott Christian University. We accept applications twice a year — September and January — across all three schools and every level of study. Start application Fees & funding Intakes January, May, September Mode of study Regular, Online Blended Application fee KSh 1 200 – 1 500 Decision in 2–3 weeks Application process Four steps to becoming a student. Most students complete the full application in under an hour. We'll guide you through each step. STEP 01 Choose your programme Browse our programmes across theology, education and TVET. Reach out to admissions if you'd like to discuss a fit. STEP 02 Submit your application Complete the online form and upload your KCSE / KCPE certificates, ID copy, two recommendations and a personal statement. STEP 03 Pay the application fee KSh 1 200 for diploma and bachelors; KSh 1 500 for masters and doctoral. Non-refundable, payable via M-Pesa or bank transfer. STEP 04 Receive your offer Decisions are issued within 2–3 weeks.

Board of Trustees Holds the assets and Christian foundation of the university in trust on behalf of the Africa Inland Church Kenya, and safeguards its mission and identity. University Council The supreme governing body for strategy, finance and policy — overseeing management, approving budgets and ensuring sound stewardship. University Senate The highest academic authority, responsible for academic policy, standards, programmes and the integrity of the university’s scholarly work. University Management The executive team led by the Vice-Chancellor, responsible for day-to-day operations, implementation of Council and Senate decisions, and strategic execution. pages.content_excerpt: +254 713 745 404 | +254 706 381 396 info@scott.ac.ke Staff Portal Student Portal Library KUCCPS Application → Home / Clubs & Activities Clubs & Activities Life at Scott Christian University goes beyond the classroom! Our vibrant clubs and student activities provide the perfect opportunity to explore your talents, build lifelong friendships, develop leadership skills, and create unforgettable memories. Whether you’re passionate about sports and games , enjoy expressing yourself through drama and creative arts , have a heart for serving others through the Hand of Compassion Club , or desire to deepen your faith by joining one of our spiritual clubs , there’s a place for you. These clubs offer exciting events, competitions, outreach programs, mentorship, community service, and fellowship throughout the academic year. They encourage teamwork, creativity, personal growth, and a strong sense of belonging within our Christ-centered community. Get involved, discover your potential, and make your university experience truly rewarding. At Scott Christian University, every student has the opportunity to learn, lead, serve, and thrive.

pages.title: Cultural Week – Scott Christian University
pages.content_excerpt: +254 713 745 404 | +254 706 381 396 info@scott.ac.ke Staff Portal Student Portal Library KUCCPS Application → Home / Cultural Week Cultural Week Celebrating Unity in Diversity Scott Christian University proudly hosts Annual Cultural Week , a vibrant celebration of the rich cultural diversity represented within our university community. Held once every year, this exciting event brings together students from different ethnic communities to showcase their unique traditions, customs, languages, music, cuisine, and heritage. Throughout the week, students participate in colorful fashion showcases , captivating traditional dances , cultural exhibitions, storytelling, and performances that highlight the beauty of Kenya’s diverse cultures and beyond. Cultural Week provides an opportunity to learn from one another, foster mutual respect, strengthen friendships, and celebrate the values of unity, inclusivity, and national cohesion. Join us as we embrace our diversity, celebrate our heritage, and create lasting memories in a spirit of love, excellence, and Christian fellowship at Scott Christian University.

pages.title: Rev. Titus Nthale – Scott Christian University
pages.content_excerpt: +254 713 745 404 | +254 706 381 396 info@scott.ac.ke Staff Portal Student Portal Library KUCCPS Application → Home / About SCU / Rev. Titus Nthale Dean of Students Rev. Titus Nthale Welcome to Scott Christian University! It is my pleasure to welcome you to our Christ-centered learning community, where academic excellence, Christian values, and servant leadership are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to providing a supportive environment that nurtures your intellectual, personal, and spiritual growth. The Dean of Students Office is dedicated to ensuring that every student has a fulfilling university experience through mentorship, student support services, leadership development, and opportunities for holistic growth. As you embark on your academic journey, I encourage you to embrace every opportunity to learn, serve, and grow. Together, let us pursue excellence and make a positive impact in our communities and beyond. Welcome to the Scott Christian University family. We wish you every success and God's abundant blessings.

Certificate in Music School of Theology > About the School > Message from the Dean > Programmes > Faculty Introduction The program is an introduction to music knowledge and practice. It introduces the learners to a broad diverse aspects of music covering the following areas: Music Theory; Introduction to voice; Introduction to history of Western music; introduction to worship; music and worship; church music administration; African culture, communication and Music; Composing songs for choir and “Praise team”; Choral Ministries; Creative and Contemporary Worship; Introduction to Musical Instruments, Introduction to Studio and Recording; and History of African Choral Music. Admission Requirements KCSE grade D+ (plus) or its equivalent No credit transfers will be provided Duration 4 months Modes of Study Day & Evening Chat with us

headings: SCHOOL OF EDUCATION AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
pages.content_excerpt: Apply Now! SCHOOL OF EDUCATION AND SOCIAL SCIENCES Established in 2012, the School of Education and Social Sciences aims at making a significant contribution towards addressing developmental challenges through quality training of personnel as well as informing policy formulation through evidence-based research output. Programmes Dean's Message Faculty About the School Incepted in 2012, the School of Education and Social Sciences seeks to offer quality programmes that not only equip students with knowledge in Social Sciences but also empowers them to be innovative and able to adopt to the dynamics in a global community. This is achieved through implementation a robust curriculum that incorporates classroom learning, research, co-curricular activities and inbuilt practicums that not only enhance acquisition of knowledge and skills in Social Science disciplines but also inculcation of values and spiritual formation. Stake holder engagement is also key to provision of a holistic education. The school collaborates with like-minded organizations, industry experts, sponsors to advance its objectives. Chat with us

REGULATIONS ON REGISTRATION REGULATIONS ON REGISTRATION Registry > Academic Calendar > Academic Scholarships > Admission Regulations > Graduation DEFINITION OF REGISTRATION REGISTRATION PROCEDURE NUMBER OF UNITS REGISTERED SEMESTER STUDENT IDENTITY CARD (ID) STUDENT EMAIL ADDRESS Registration is the formal admission of a student to a programme of study, or research, leading to a degree of the university or to any academic award for which a degree or other approved form of qualification is a necessary entry condition. An Academic Year Upon admission, a student is enrolled for an academic year. Limuru Campus has two major semesters (of 15 weeks) and semester three which is optional (of 10 weeks): August to December 1 st Semester January to April 2 nd Semester May to July (Optional) 3 rd term Nairobi, Nakuru and Machakos campuses have three equal trimesters, 12 weeks each. Full fees for each semester must be paid in order for a student to study in a given semester. REGISTRATION PERIOD The official registration period is one week. He has served at Taita Taveta University since 2015 and was the founding Dean, School of Science and Informatics. His research interests are in the field of Water and Wastewater Treatment Technologies, Soil Chemistry and Atmospheric Pollution studies. Prof. Maghanga has vast Industrial experience having previously worked in the fields of; refractories, steel production, paint formulations and black tea production quality control. Prof. Maghanga has professional membership with the Royal Society of Chemistry, Environmental Institute of Kenya, Chemical Society of Kenya and Pan African Chemical Society. pages.content_excerpt: Online Application Portal Log in Create account Programmes Help ACCOUNTING TECHNICIANS DIPLOMA (ATD) COURSE LEVEL 1 Part I - When to Join Any time Part II - Requirements The minimum entry for the diploma courses is KCSE mean grade C-. Persons with certificate and other higher qualifications from recognized institutions are also eligible for entry. Part III - Approximate Fees & Projected Study Schedule Duration: 4 Months Cost (in KES):24000 *This excludes Industrial Attachment/Industrial-Based Learning. **The University reserves the right to implement fees changes approved by the University Council without prior notice. Part IV - Where Offered Department ACCOUNTING AND FINANCE School BUSINESS AND MANAGEMENT STUDIES Faculty SOCIAL SCIENCES AND TECHNOLOGY Part V - Interested in the Programme? If you are interested in this programme, then start by creating an account with us or signing in , if the account is already created, in order to apply for this programme. Not Interested in this Programme? You Can Search for Other Programmes below: Programmes on Offer GO HINT: Search using unique terms like civil, electrical, computer, business, accounting, chemistry, biology, mathematics, psycho

Prof. Sagwa is an accomplished department chair with over 25 years of experience in academic leadership, programme design and development, proven track record of enhancing curriculum, fostering faculty collaboration and enhancing student success in a dynamic education environment. Prof. Sagwa has played major roles in identifying and mapping out stakeholders for partnership engagement at the Technical University. He has sat in Research Committees guiding national policy and institutional frameworks for integration and collaboration, designed programmes for facilitation of access of the university to small business communities surrounding the university as well as programs for leading students to commercialization of emerging involved in championing the establishment of an innovation and technology Hub at the Technical University of Kenya. pages.content_excerpt: Certificate in Information Communication Technology and Computer Maintenance Certificate in Information Communication Technology and Computer Maintenance Overview The Certificate in ICT and Computer Maintenance (CICM) programme is designed to train competent computer technologists who can respond to societal needs through the use of computer applications, software development, computer networks, and computer systems maintenance. The programme is motivated by the need to impart technical skills that meet industry and business requirements, particularly in computer networks and computer maintenance. It also provides opportunities for students pursuing technical courses in Information Technology to advance their careers, acquire practical skills to adapt to changes in the ICT industry, and progress to further training. The programme aims to equip trainees with the necessary skills to install and maintain computer networks and carry out maintenance work on computer systems. The programme normally extends over two academic years, comprising four semesters of sixteen weeks each. It consists of 21 course units, including an internal attachment of at least eight weeks. pages.content_excerpt: Application Guide Apply online, step by step. Part One Student Online Application 1 Enter smis.tum.ac.ke/application/register in the browser to access the registration page. The TUMMIS sign-in page will display. 2 Click the register link. This will display the create TUMMIS account page. 3 Enter your email, mobile number, password and the security captcha value, then click create account. 4 An email is sent to the applicant's account on how to activate the account. 5 Click the tab displayed to activate your account. The login page is now displayed. 6 Enter the email and password used to create the account. 7 Log in using the credentials used to create the account. The system will open a page requiring a verification code sent to your mobile phone number. 8 Enter the verification code from your mobile phone and click the Verify Phone Number button. 9 The system will open a page requiring you to update your personal details - title, first name, middle name, surname, gender and date of birth. 10 Enter your personal information and click the Submit and Continue button. 11 Enter your contact information and click the Submit and Continue button. 12 Enter your address information and clic

Entry Requirements Find the grade you need Admission to the Technical University of Mombasa is competitive and based on merit. For certain courses, specific subjects may also be taken into consideration - always confirm the cluster requirements for your chosen programme. 01 Certificate Minimum of Mean Grade D+ in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (K.C.S.E) or equivalent qualifications. 02 Diploma Minimum of Mean Grade C- in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (K.C.S.E) or equivalent qualifications. 03 Undergraduate Minimum of Mean Grade C+ in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (K.C.S.E) or equivalent qualifications. 04 Postgraduate - Master's A Bachelor's degree with a minimum of Second Class Honours Upper Division or its equivalent in the relevant field from a recognized institution. 05 Postgraduate - Doctoral A Master's degree from a recognized institution in a relevant field. pages.content_excerpt: Tharaka University (TUN) successfully held the 4th Edition of its Annual Cultural Week from 13th to 16th October 2025, themed “Leveraging Cultural Diversities for Patriotism and National Cohesion.” The week-long celebration brought together students, staff, and guests from across the country to showcase Kenya’s rich cultural heritage through traditional performances, cultural exhibitions, and creative displays. The event’s grand finale was graced by the Vice-Chancellor and CEO, Prof. Peter K. Muriungi, who led the awarding ceremony and emphasized the importance of cultural preservation. Quoting Marcus Garvey, he noted, “A people without knowledge of their past history, origin and culture is like a tree without roots.” Prof. Muriungi added that culture remains relevant in contemporary society, highlighting how nations like Japan and China continue to embrace their traditions while driving innovation and development. Tharaka University continues to uphold its commitment to fostering unity in diversity, patriotism, and national cohesion through such cultural initiatives. Jan 27, 2025 Knowledge Tags Education , Knowledge , Learning , University About the Author webmaster

The initiative seeks to promote the study, preservation, and use of the Kîîtharaka language by making books and other learning materials accessible through the Tharaka University E-Library platform, supporting scholars, students, and pupils interested in indigenous language studies. During his time abroad, Mwaura worked in specialized laboratories at the Fort Hare Institute of Technology (FHIT), focusing on the development and characterization of thin films, key materials used in solar panels and other photovoltaic systems for sustainable energy harvesting. While in South Africa, Mr. Mwaura also participated in UFH’s Research Week of Excellence, where he engaged with distinguished scholars and explored emerging ideas in his field. This research visit formed part of an academic exchange program made possible courtesy of the strong and ongoing collaborative partnership between the University of Fort Hare and Tharaka University. The visit was hosted by Prof. Edson Meyer of the University of Fort Hare, whose role was instrumental in facilitating the research exchange, and has been working closely with Dr. Fidelis Ngugi, Dean of the Faculty of Physical Sciences, Engineering, and Technology (FPET) at Tharaka University. pages.content_excerpt: Tharaka University (TUN) held a Coffee Meet-up community engagement activity with parents of Mukothima sub-county to discuss the challenges and attitudes around the learning and use of the Kîîtharaka language in schools and the community. The activity, which was held at the Little City (Mukothima) is part of the research project: Minoritized language attitudes overcoming local challenges in the use and teaching of Kîîtharaka as an indigenous Language in schools and in the broader community. During the engagement, Dr. Kanampiu, the local Project Lead, took participants through the myths surrounding learning multiple languages and the benefits of multilingualism. He stressed that learning of indigenous languages alongside other majority languages like English and Kiswahili does not cause confusion or delay the learning of English or Kiswahili. “Research evidence shows that children learn mathematics and acquire literacy skills much earlier, if these are delivered in a language they understand and speak,” Dr. Kanampiu explained. pages.content_excerpt: Tharaka University (TUN) Vice-Chancellor and CEO, Prof. Peter K. Muriungi, today received a delegation of opinion leaders from Chiakariga Ward, who paid a courtesy call to his office ahead of discussing the expansion of higher education in the region. During the engagement, the leaders formally presented their aspirations and lobbied for the establishment of a Tunyai, Tharaka University campus in the Chiakariga–Mariene area. They highlighted the region’s strategic location, the growing number of students seeking university education, and the significant socio-economic benefits that a university campus would bring to the local community, including improved access to higher education, employment opportunities, and accelerated regional development. Prof. Muriungi welcomed the delegation and commended them for their proactive engagement with the University. He affirmed that Tharaka University values inclusive consultations with community stakeholders and emphasized that the proposal would be subjected to the relevant institutional frameworks and government approval processes. pages.content_excerpt: Tharaka University today proudly held its annual inauguration ceremony for the 2026/2027 Student Leadership body, marking a key milestone in strengthening student governance and leadership within the institution. The ceremony brought together university management, staff, and students to witness the newly elected student leaders (TUSA) as they assume office. The Vice-Chancellor emphasized that leadership is anchored on responsibility rather than visibility, noting that the electoral process continues to nurture a culture of accountability and responsible governance among students. The Chairperson of the Electoral Commission, Dr. Collins Sitienei, applauded the student body for demonstrating maturity, peace, and responsibility throughout the electoral process. The ceremony also celebrated outstanding sporting achievements by Tharaka University teams, including remarkable performances in rugby, para-athletics, darts, taekwondo, and basketball, reflecting the university’s commitment to holistic student development. Located in the serene town of Kitengela, Kajiado County, TEAU is recognized and accredited by the Commission for University Education (CUE), a testament to its academic excellence, robust governance, and commitment to national development. Strategically situated along the Nairobi-Kajiado-Namanga Highway, the university enjoys a unique location within the Nairobi Metropolitan region. TEAU is just 10 kilometers south of Kitengela town and about 40 kilometers from Nairobi’s Central Business District. The university is also conveniently connected to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA)—a gateway for international students and scholars—making it a global academic hub in the heart of East Africa Discover your potential. pages.content_excerpt: Home Academics Undergraduate BACHELOR OF ARTS (ECONOMICS, WITH I.T.) BACHELOR OF ARTS (ECONOMICS, WITH I.T.) Faculty of Business and Economics Undergraduate Course Description This program focuses on economic theory, policy, and analysis, combined with practical I.T. skills for data management and research. It prepares students to understand and solve economic issues in a digital world. Expectations Over the 4-year full-time course, students are expected to develop strong analytical, quantitative, and digital skills. A high level of discipline, critical thinking, and the ability to apply economic concepts using technology is essential. Participation in research, policy analysis, and ethical decision-making is emphasized throughout the program. Market Areas Graduates can work in financial institutions, government departments, economic research, consultancy firms, NGOs, and data-driven roles in both public and private sectors. Minimum Requirements KCSE MEAN GRADE C+ OR HIGHER, (C OR HIGHER REQUIRED IN MATHEMATICS) OR A DIPLOMA IN BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION OR RELATED COURSE FROM AN ACCREDITED INSTITUTION. OR IGCSE SIX B’S INCLUDING MATHEMATICS AND ENGLISH AND A LEVEL 2 PRINCIPAL PASSES

pages.content_excerpt: Home Academics Undergraduate BACHELOR OF SCIENCE (HEALTH RECORDS & INFORMATION MANAGEMENT, WITH I.T.) BACHELOR OF SCIENCE (HEALTH RECORDS & INFORMATION MANAGEMENT, WITH I.T.) Faculty of Physical and Biological Sciences Undergraduate Course Description This program integrates health information management with modern IT solutions to transform healthcare data systems. Students will master medical records management, health data standards, and digital health technologies while developing expertise in healthcare informatics, database management, and data security protocols. Expectations Students will develop expertise in leading health information systems like EPIC and Cerner, while mastering essential medical coding standards (ICD-10, CPT). The program emphasizes healthcare data analytics, information visualization techniques, and HIPAA-compliant data security practices. Graduates will gain practical skills in healthcare database management, preparing them to handle sensitive medical information effectively in digital environments. Market Areas Graduates can pursue rewarding careers as health information managers in hospitals and clinics, ensuring efficient medical records management.

headings: Faculty of Physical and Biological Sciences
pages.content_excerpt: Tom Mboya University Faculty of Physical and Biological Sciences Leadership Message from the Dean This Faculty houses programs in Biological, Physical and Earth Sciences including Agriculture. The faculty is dedicated to helping students become lifelong learners and preparing them for careers in the rapidly emerging knowledge-based economy. Through the active professional development of its faculty and the use of state-of-the-art science laboratories, it has enhanced learning environment. Students in this faculty have demonstrated their value in a number of initiatives, including the Presidential Digital Talent Program, which has helped many of them land on jobs fast. Due to the high skills demonstrated, many employers have absorbed our students in organizations where they underwent their industrial attachments. DR. IRENE OKELLO, PhD. pages.content_excerpt: Tom Mboya University CMG Argwings Kodhek Faculty of Law Leadership Message from the Dean Welcome to the Faculty of Law. It gives me great pleasure to welcome you to a dynamic and forward-looking academic environment committed to excellence in legal education, research, and professional development. Our Faculty is dedicated to nurturing competent, ethical, and innovative legal professionals who are well equipped to respond to the evolving demands of society. In recognition of the rapid integration of technology in all spheres of life, we offer programmes such as the Bachelor of Laws (LL.B) with Information Technology, designed to prepare graduates for a modern, digital legal landscape. Our curriculum blends strong theoretical foundations with practical skills, ensuring that our students are not only knowledgeable in the law but also adaptable to emerging technological trends. We pride ourselves on a student-centered approach, experienced faculty, and a commitment to integrity, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. Tom Mboya University Faculty of Education Leadership Message from the Dean The faculty of Education is one of the pioneer faculties in Tom Mboya university that was created in September 2018. The Faculty houses three (3) Undergraduate and twelve (12) post graduate programmes. The programmes are mounted as regular, evening, weekend and holidays/recess depending on quorum in a calendar year. The faculty is responsive to the everchanging curricula in the whole education system and related undertakings in the society. Dr. Joab M. Kinzi, PhD. Faculty of Education fedu@tmu.ac.ke Foundation Vision, Mission & Mandate Vision Faculty of Education strives to be a center of excellence dedicated to teaching, research, mentorship and partnership with both local and global communities. Mission Our mission is to foster excellence in teaching, research, and learning with the view to produce responsible graduates capable of transforming our society. Mandate Our mandate is drawn from the University College's Statutes guided by the Universities Act, 2012. pages.content_excerpt: Tom Mboya University Health Care Quality, accessible health care services for our university community — students, staff, and their families. Health Department Message from the Head of Department The university recognizes that the Health Department at all levels is key in the provision of quality health care services to the stakeholders. Guided by the university policies and being a government-approved facility, it is in this regard that the department has continued to provide holistic health care services to both staff and students. The department is committed to effectively discharging its functions, among others: Clinical services, Nursing services, Laboratory services, Medical Records, Pharmacy, Ambulance services, and Counselling services. The Health Department warmly welcomes you to Tom Mboya University. Milka Wasonga Head of Health Department Our Services Health Care Services Comprehensive medical services available to the TMU community. pages.content_excerpt: Games and Sports Games and Sports Life at Tom Mboya University is enriching, exciting, and energizing. Head of Sports 🏆 Message from the HOD Welcome to the Sports and Games Department at Tom Mboya University. As the Head of Department, I take pride in fostering a vibrant and inclusive sporting culture that nurtures talent, promotes physical fitness, and enhances the overall well-being of our students. Our department offers a variety of athletic disciplines, ranging from competitive team sports to recreational activities, all designed to empower students both on and off the field. We are committed to identifying and developing potential, encouraging teamwork, and instilling values of discipline and perseverance. The Department welcomes you to Tom Mboya University. pages.content_excerpt: University of Eastern Africa, Baraton Confers Honorary Doctorate on President William Samoei Ruto By Dr. Nathan Gitonga, UEAB Media Baraton, August 18, 2024: This morning, His Excellency Dr William Samoei Ruto, President of the Republic of Kenya, was awarded a Doctor of Humane Letters in Leadership, Honoris Causa. The distinction has been granted by the institution through its Statute XXIII, paragraph 3, upon the recommendation of Senate and approval by the University Council. The honorary degree was bequeathed by the university’s Chancellor, Dr. Blasious Ruguri, who also serves as the President of the East-Central Africa Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The citation describing the remarkable achievements of Dr. Ruto was read by the Vice Chancellor of the University, Prof. Jackson Mmamba Msafiri, PhD, which hit home just how momentous this was. In his acceptance speech, President Ruto made a stunning declaration: this was the first time he had accepted an honorary degree from any university in the world. pages.content_excerpt: Application Procedures In order to avoid delay in the processing of applications and giving the students ample time to prepare to join the university, applicants are advised to submit application forms and supporting documents to the Office of the Assistant Registrar for Admission at least one (1) month prior to the anticipated date of entry. An applicant seeking admission into a graduate program should submit a completed application form and the following supporting documents: Official receipt of payment of a non-refundable application fee of KSh 2,500 (US$ 26.00). Certified photocopies of college or university diplomas or certificates. Two (2) recent passport-size photos. Three (3) filled evaluation (recommendation) forms for graduate studies from referees in sealed envelopes. Note: Referees must not be blood-related to the applicant and must know his/her professional abilities and personal character very well. Two (2) certified copies of official transcripts from each college and university attended. Certified photocopy of secondary school certificate. Updated curriculum vitae.
